title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable quantum communication, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in metropolitan distances.
method: The review surveys CV quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) protocols, including Gaussian-modulated coherent states and discrete modulation, security proofs against collective and coherent attacks, and experimental implementations with homodyne/heterodyne detection.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and secret key rates, with security proofs now covering finite-size effects and composable security. The review also discusses measurement-device-independent and twin-field CV-QKD variants.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and rapidly advancing field, with practical systems deployed in real-world networks and strong theoretical foundations.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging conventional methods and providing new insights.

title: Decoupling Local Classicality From Classical Explainability: A Noncontextual Model For Bilocal Classical Theory And A Locally-classical But Contextual Theory
authors: Sina Soltani, Marco Erba, David Schmid, And John H.selby
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2142 (2026).

We construct an ontological model for the theory known as bilocal classical theory [1]. To our knowledge, this is only the second time that an ontological model has been constructed for an entire theory, rather than just for some particular scenarios within a theory. This result refutes a conjecture from [1] which suggested that there might be no local-realist ontological model for bilocal classical theory. Moreover, it is the first time that an ontological model has been constructed for a theory that fails to be locally tomographic, showing that the assumption of local tomography underpinning the structure theorem in [2] is a genuine limitation of the theorem. This demonstrates that in general there is no tension between failures of local tomography and classical explainability (i.e., generalised noncontextuality). In fact, bilocal classical theory is in many ways more simply understood via the underlying ontological model than it is within its original formulation (much as how odd-dimensional stabiliser subtheories can be more simply understood via Spekkens' toy theory). Furthermore, this result naturally leads to the question, does every locally-classical theory admit of an ontological model? By constructing a concrete counterexample, we show that this is not the case. Our findings demonstrate that there is no straightforward relationship between theories being locally-classical, and them being classically-explainable. This shows that the fundamental status of compositional properties (such as local tomography) is not a technical side-issue, but a central and unavoidable question for a coherent understanding even of classicality itself.

.
tldr: Constructs an ontological model for bilocal classical theory, refuting a conjecture and showing that local classicality does not imply classical explainability.
motivation: To understand the relationship between local tomography, local classicality, and generalized noncontextuality, and to test whether every locally-classical theory admits an ontological model.
method: Constructs an explicit ontological model for bilocal classical theory using a hidden variable framework, and then builds a counterexample theory that is locally-classical but contextual.
result: Bilocal classical theory has a local-realist ontological model, contrary to a previous conjecture; moreover, there exists a locally-classical theory that is contextual, decoupling the two properties.
conclusion: Local classicality does not guarantee classical explainability (generalized noncontextuality), highlighting the importance of compositional properties like local tomography for understanding classicality.

title: Measurement Incompatibility And Quantum Steering Via Linear Programming
authors: Lucas E. A. Porto, Sébastien Designolle, Sebastian Pokutta, And Marco Túlio Quintino
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2141 (2026).

The problem of deciding whether a set of quantum measurements is jointly measurable is known to be equivalent to determining whether a quantum assemblage is unsteerable. This problem can be formulated as a semidefinite program (SDP). However, the number of variables and constraints in such a formulation grows exponentially with the number of measurements, rendering it intractable for large measurement sets. In this work, we circumvent this problem by transforming the SDP into a hierarchy of linear programs that compute upper and lower bounds on the incompatibility robustness with a complexity that grows polynomially in the number of measurements. The hierarchy is guaranteed to converge and it can be applied to arbitrary measurements – including non-projective POVMs (Positive Operator-Valued Measures) – in arbitrary dimensions. While convergence becomes impractical in high dimensions, in the case of qubits our method reliably provides accurate upper and lower bounds for the incompatibility robustness of sets with several hundred measurements in a short time using a standard laptop. We also apply our methods to qutrits, obtaining non-trivial upper and lower bounds in scenarios that are otherwise intractable using the standard SDP approach, although such bounds are significantly looser than the ones obtained in the qubit case. Finally, we show how our methods can be used to construct local hidden state models for states (i.e., to prove that a state cannot lead to steering under any possible local measurements), or conversely, to certify that a given state exhibits steering; for two-qubit quantum states, our approach is comparable to, and in some cases outperforms, the current best methods.

.
tldr: This paper transforms the semidefinite program for joint measurability and steering into a hierarchy of linear programs, enabling efficient computation of bounds for large measurement sets.
motivation: The standard SDP for deciding joint measurability and steering becomes intractable for large measurement sets due to exponential growth in variables and constraints.
method: The authors reformulate the SDP as a hierarchy of linear programs that provide upper and lower bounds on incompatibility robustness, with polynomial complexity in the number of measurements.
result: For qubits, the method yields accurate bounds for sets with hundreds of measurements quickly; for qutrits, non-trivial bounds are obtained where SDP fails. The approach also constructs local hidden state models for steering.
conclusion: The linear programming hierarchy offers a practical tool for analyzing measurement incompatibility and quantum steering in large scenarios, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Tight Bounds For Quantum Phase Estimation And Related Problems
authors: Nikhil S. Mande And Ronald de Wolf
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2140 (2026).

Phase estimation, due to Kitaev [17], is one of the most fundamental subroutines in quantum computing. In the basic scenario, one is given black-box access to a unitary [MATH], and an eigenstate [MATH] of [MATH] with unknown eigenvalue [MATH], and the task is to estimate the eigenphase [MATH] within [MATH], with high probability. The cost of an algorithm for us is the number of applications of [MATH] and [MATH]. We tightly characterize the cost of several variants of phase estimation where we are no longer given an eigenstate, but are required to estimate the maximum eigenphase of [MATH], aided by advice in the form of states (or a unitary preparing those states) which are promised to have at least a certain overlap [MATH] with the top eigenspace. We give algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds for all ranges of parameters. We show that a small number of copies of the advice state (or of an advice-preparing unitary) are not significantly better than having no advice at all. We also show that having lots of advice (applications of the advice-preparing unitary) does not significantly reduce cost, and neither does knowledge of the eigenbasis of [MATH]. We immediately obtain a lower bound on the complexity of the Unitary recurrence time problem, resolving an open question of She and Yuen [29]. Lastly, we study how efficiently one can reduce the error probability in the basic phase-estimation scenario. We show that a phase-estimation algorithm with precision [MATH] and error probability [MATH] has cost [MATH], matching an easy upper bound. This contrasts with some other scenarios in quantum computing (e.g., search) where error-probability reduction costs only a factor [MATH]. Our lower bound uses a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials.

.
tldr: This paper tightly characterizes the query complexity of quantum phase estimation with advice states, providing nearly matching upper and lower bounds for all parameter regimes.
motivation: Phase estimation is a fundamental subroutine in quantum computing, but its cost when given imperfect advice (states with partial overlap with the top eigenspace) was not well understood. Understanding this helps optimize quantum algorithms and resolve open problems like the unitary recurrence time.
method: The authors develop algorithms for phase estimation with advice and prove lower bounds using the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials, as well as reductions from the unitary recurrence time problem.
result: They show that a small number of advice copies are not significantly better than no advice, and that many advice applications do not reduce cost much. They also prove that error probability reduction costs a factor of 1/ε, matching an easy upper bound.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the cost of phase estimation with advice, resolving open questions and offering tight bounds that will guide algorithm design.

title: Qudit Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Inequality And Nonlocality From Wigner Negativity
authors: Uta Isabella Meyer, Ivan Šupić, Damian Markham, And Frédéric Grosshans
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2139 (2026).

Nonlocality is an essential concept that distinguishes quantum from classical models and has been extensively studied in systems of qubits. For higher-dimensional systems, certain results for their two-level counterpart, like Bell violations with stabilizer states and Clifford operators, do not generalize. On the other hand, similar to continuous variable systems, Wigner negativity is necessary for nonlocality in qudit systems. We propose a new generalization of the CHSH inequality for qudits by inquiring correlations related to the Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalization of the qubit [MATH]-gate. A specified stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality among all qudit states based on its Wigner negativity. The Bell operator not only serves as a measure for the singlet fraction but also quantifies the volume of Wigner negativity. Additionally, we show how a bipartite entangled qudit state can serve as a witness for contextuality when it exhibits Wigner negativity. Furthermore, we identify rational-phase diagonal unitaries as the key resource that exactly reproduce the CGLMP and SATWAP violation with the maximally entangled state through simple phase-difference alignment.

.
tldr: Proposes a qudit CHSH inequality based on Wigner negativity, showing that stabilizer states with maximal Wigner negativity achieve maximal violation, and connects the Bell operator to singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume.
motivation: Generalizing Bell inequalities to higher-dimensional systems is challenging because known qubit results do not directly extend; this work aims to establish a connection between nonlocality and Wigner negativity in qudit systems.
method: The authors introduce a new CHSH-like inequality for qudits using correlations derived from Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalized π/8 gate, and analyze the Bell operator's properties.
result: A specific stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality, with violation quantified by its Wigner negativity; the Bell operator measures both singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume; bipartite entangled qudit states with Wigner negativity witness contextuality.
conclusion: Wigner negativity is a necessary resource for nonlocality in qudit systems, and the proposed inequality provides a direct operational link between nonlocality and negativity, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Device-independent Secure Correlations In Sequential Quantum Scenarios
authors: Matteo Padovan, Alessandro Rezzi, And Lorenzo Coccia
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2131 (2026).

Device-independent quantum information is attracting significant attention, particularly for its applications in information security. This interest arises because the security of device-independent protocols relies solely on the observed outcomes of spatially separated measurements and the validity of quantum physics. Sequential scenarios, i.e., where measurements occur in a precise temporal order, have been proved to enhance performance of device-independent protocols in some specific cases by enabling the reuse of the same quantum state. In this work, we propose a systematic approach to designing sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security. Our method begins with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and transforms it into a sequential protocol by replacing one measurement with its non-projective counterpart and adding an additional user thereafter. We analytically prove that, with this systematic construction, the resulting ideal correlations are secure in the sense that they cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, thereby enabling, for example, the device-independent certification of all the randomness present in the observed correlations. The general recipe we provide can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum schemes for security.

.
tldr: A systematic method to design sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security, starting from bipartite self-testing qubit protocols.
motivation: Device-independent protocols rely on observed outcomes and quantum physics, and sequential scenarios can enhance performance by reusing quantum states; a general construction method is needed.
method: Replace one measurement in a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol with a non-projective counterpart and add an additional user, then prove the resulting correlations are secure.
result: The constructed ideal correlations cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, enabling device-independent certification of randomness.
conclusion: The general recipe can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum security schemes.

title: Detecting Entanglement By State Preparation And Local Measurements
authors: Jaemin Kim, Anindita Bera, Dariusz Chruściński, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2128 (2026).

Entanglement witnesses (EWs) are a collection of observables that can characterize separable states and, experimentally, estimating EWs can verify entangled states. In this work, we show that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite entangled state, which we introduce as a network state for the purpose, can estimate EWs. Namely, entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner, in which experimenters do not necessarily change measurement settings. We present a fixed measurement setting and network states for estimating decomposable EWs, equivalent to the partial transpose criteria. We also consider non-decomposable EWs that detect bound entangled states beyond the partial transpose criteria. The results can be extended to multipartite states such as graph states, a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, and readily applied to distributed settings such as quantum metrology or sensor networks where multipartite entangled states are resourceful.

.
tldr: A fixed measurement setting on a multipartite network state can estimate entanglement witnesses, enabling measurement-based entanglement verification without changing measurement settings.
motivation: Entanglement witnesses are crucial for verifying entanglement but typically require different measurement settings for each witness. The authors aim to simplify experimental verification by using a fixed measurement setting.
method: The authors introduce a network state and a fixed measurement setting that can estimate decomposable entanglement witnesses (equivalent to partial transpose criteria) and non-decomposable ones for bound entangled states. They extend the method to multipartite graph states.
result: The proposed scheme can fully verify entangled states in a measurement-based manner, applicable to distributed settings like quantum metrology and sensor networks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, measurement-efficient approach to entanglement detection, relevant for quantum information processing and networking.

title: A Local Automaton For The 2d Toric Code
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, And Ethan Lake
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2125 (2026).

We construct a local decoder for the 2D toric code using ideas from the hierarchical classical cellular automata of Tsirelson and Gács. Our decoder is a circuit of strictly local quantum operations preserving a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise without the need for non-local classical computation or communication. Our construction is not translation invariant in spacetime, but can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes. This solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.

.
tldr: Constructs a local decoder for the 2D toric code that preserves logical state for exponential time using hierarchical cellular automata.
motivation: To solve the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions without non-local classical computation.
method: Uses ideas from hierarchical classical cellular automata (Tsirelson and Gács) to design a strictly local quantum circuit decoder for the 2D toric code.
result: The decoder preserves a logical state for exponential time under circuit-level noise, and can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes.
conclusion: Demonstrates that local topological quantum memory is possible in 2D, resolving a long-standing open problem.

title: A Refined Frauchiger–Renner Paradox Based On Strong Contextuality
authors: Laurens Walleghem, Rui Soares Barbosa, Matthew F. Pusey, And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2116 (2026).

The Frauchiger–Renner paradox derives an inconsistency when quantum theory is used to describe the use of itself, by means of a scenario where agents model other agents quantumly and reason about each other's knowledge. We observe that logical contextuality (à la Hardy) is the key ingredient of the FR paradox, and we provide a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario. In contrast to the FR paradox, this GHZ–FR paradox neither requires post-selection nor any reasoning by observers who are modelled quantumly. If one accepts the universality of quantum theory including superobservers, we propose a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve these extended Wigner's friend paradoxes.

.
tldr: The paper strengthens the Frauchiger–Renner paradox by linking it to strong contextuality in the GHZ–Mermin scenario, eliminating the need for post-selection or quantum reasoning by agents.
motivation: The Frauchiger–Renner paradox highlights inconsistencies in quantum theory when applied to itself, but its reliance on post-selection and agent reasoning has been criticized. The authors aim to provide a cleaner paradox based on logical contextuality.
method: The authors observe that the FR paradox is a form of logical contextuality à la Hardy and then construct a stronger paradox using the GHZ–Mermin scenario, which is known to be strongly contextual. They analyze the new GHZ–FR paradox without post-selection or quantum reasoning by agents.
result: The GHZ–FR paradox is derived, showing a contradiction that does not require post-selection or agents reasoning about each other's quantum states, relying solely on strong contextuality.
conclusion: The paradox reinforces the foundational issues in quantum theory and suggests a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve extended Wigner's friend paradoxes.

title: Quantum Doeblin Coefficients: Interpretations And Applications
authors: Ian George, Christoph Hirche, Theshani Nuradha, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2115 (2026).

In classical information theory, the Doeblin coefficient of a classical channel provides an efficiently computable upper bound on the total-variation contraction coefficient of the channel, leading to what is known as a strong data-processing inequality. Here, we investigate quantum Doeblin coefficients as a generalization of the classical concept. In particular, we define various new quantum Doeblin coefficients, one of which has several desirable properties, including concatenation and multiplicativity, in addition to being efficiently computable. We also develop various interpretations of two of the quantum Doeblin coefficients, including representations as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, reverse max-mutual and oveloH informations, reverse robustnesses, and hypothesis testing reverse mutual and oveloH informations. Our interpretations of quantum Doeblin coefficients as either entanglement-assisted or unassisted exclusion values are particularly appealing, indicating that they are proportional to the best possible error probabilities one could achieve in state-exclusion tasks by making use of the channel. We also outline various applications of quantum Doeblin coefficients, ranging from limitations on quantum machine learning algorithms that use parameterized quantum circuits (noise-induced barren plateaus), on error mitigation protocols, on the sample complexity of noisy quantum hypothesis testing, on the fairness of noisy quantum models, and on mixing, indistinguishability, and decoupling times of time-varying channels. All of these applications make use of the fact that quantum Doeblin coefficients appear in upper bounds on various trace-distance contraction coefficients of a quantum channel. Furthermore, in all of these applications, our analysis using quantum Doeblin coefficients provides improvements of various kinds over contributions from prior literature, both in terms of generality and being efficiently computable.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum Doeblin coefficients as a generalization of classical Doeblin coefficients, providing efficiently computable upper bounds on trace-distance contraction coefficients of quantum channels with applications to noise-induced barren plateaus, error mitigation, and hypothesis testing.
motivation: Classical Doeblin coefficients provide strong data-processing inequalities, but a quantum generalization with desirable properties like multiplicativity and efficient computability was lacking.
method: The authors define several quantum Doeblin coefficients, prove their properties (concatenation, multiplicativity, efficient computability), and derive interpretations in terms of minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, and reverse mutual informations.
result: The quantum Doeblin coefficients are shown to be proportional to optimal error probabilities in state-exclusion tasks, and they yield improved upper bounds on trace-distance contraction coefficients, leading to applications in quantum machine learning, error mitigation, and hypothesis testing.
conclusion: Quantum Doeblin coefficients are a versatile tool for bounding contraction coefficients, with broad applications and improvements over prior work in generality and computability.

title: Optimal Control Of Engineered Swift Equilibration Of Nanomechanical Oscillators
authors: Julia Sanders And Paolo Muratore-Ginanneschi
abstract: Processes conveying physical information are always subject to speed limits. We explore the consequence of this in optimal control of indicators of finite-time thermodynamic transitions of nano-systems evolving according to an underdamped dynamics. Our main finding is that, in the presence of speed limits, problems like optimal engineered swift equilibration and transitions towards an out-of-equilibrium state at minimum work done to the system are well-posed. In particular, we show that there is no need for discontinuities in the internal energy at the end of the control horizon. This was a problem that raised doubts for a long time on the physical meaning of certain optimal transitions. We perform our analysis on the experimentally relevant case of nano-oscillators, and we expect our predictions on optimal protocols and the evolution of mean heat and work to be experimentally testable.
tldr: This paper studies optimal control of engineered swift equilibration for nanomechanical oscillators under speed limits, showing that finite-time thermodynamic transitions can be well-posed without internal energy discontinuities.
motivation: Processes conveying physical information are subject to speed limits, and optimal control of finite-time thermodynamic transitions in nano-systems has been hindered by apparent need for discontinuities in internal energy.
method: The authors analyze optimal control of underdamped nanomechanical oscillators, deriving protocols for swift equilibration and out-of-equilibrium transitions that minimize work, using speed-limit constraints.
result: They prove that optimal engineered swift equilibration and minimum-work transitions are well-posed without internal energy discontinuities, resolving a long-standing doubt.
conclusion: The predicted optimal protocols and evolution of mean heat and work are experimentally testable on nano-oscillators, advancing quantum thermodynamics of small systems.

title: Precise Computation Of Universal Corner Entanglement Entropy At 2+1 Dimension: From Ising To Gaussian Quantum Critical Points
authors: Ben Lee-Yeung Ngai, Justin Tim-Lok Chau, Junchen Rong, Meng Cheng, Yuan Da Liao And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in the entanglement entropy (EE) of (2+1)d quantum many-body systems remains a significant challenge, despite its central role in revealing universal information about quantum states and quantum critical points (QCPs). Building on recent algorithmic advances that enable the stable calculation of EE as an exponential observable (Zhou et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 165106; Zhang et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 205147; Liao et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B110 235111), we develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) algorithm to precisely and efficiently compute the universal corner of EE at QCPs in a (2+1)d square-lattice transverse-field Ising model augmented with a four-body interaction. Turning on this interaction allows us to trace an Ising critical line, reaching the tricritical point, and then a line of first-order phase transition. In (2+1)d, the tricritical point is described by the Gaussian theory, where a theoretical calculation of the corner logarithmic term in the 2nd Rényi entropy term is available (Casini and Huerta 2007 Nucl. Phys. B764 183). Our QMC results are in quantitative agreement with this theoretical value, providing a highly nontrivial benchmark of the algorithm. Furthermore, we also study the Rényi EE at the Ising critical line and on the first-order transition line, obtaining results consistent with theoretical expectations. These findings establish the long-sought connection between the universal values of an exactly solvable limit and those of a strongly correlated regime at (2+1)d.
tldr: This paper computes the universal corner entanglement entropy at (2+1)d quantum critical points using a novel QMC algorithm, achieving quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions.
motivation: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in entanglement entropy for (2+1)d systems is challenging but crucial for revealing universal information about quantum states and critical points.
method: The authors develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo algorithm to compute the 2nd Rényi entropy as an exponential observable, applied to a square-lattice transverse-field Ising model with a four-body interaction.
result: The QMC results match the theoretical corner logarithmic term for the Gaussian tricritical point, and also provide consistent results for the Ising critical line and first-order transition line.
conclusion: The algorithm successfully bridges the gap between exactly solvable limits and strongly correlated regimes, establishing a long-sought connection for universal corner entanglement entropy in (2+1)d.

title: Borrowed Identities: Malleable Distillation Factories And A Unified Numerical Search
authors: Shraddha Singh, Craig Gidney, Cody Jones
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magic-state distillation is one of the leading overheads in fault-tolerant quantum computation. Existing methods for finding distillation factories require a transversal gate to act correctly on the entire codespace, a constraint that limits both generality and search efficiency. We introduce a strictly weaker borrowed-identity condition, requiring only that the distillation circuit act as the identity on a single input state. It applies uniformly across all levels of the Clifford hierarchy and unifies, within a single level, factories that distill different magic states -- for example, the [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] factories. A brute-force search over borrowed-identity circuits with two-group symmetry recovers, within the search range, all distance-2 factories known from code-construction approaches, including entangled-output and multi-output factories previously outside the scope of any single numerical search. This unification yields parent circuits that encode multiple factories, so the output magic-state type can be chosen at compile time rather than fixed by a hard-coded design. The framework also extends beyond CSS codes, unifying constructions, including synthillation and non-CSS catalytic factories, previously obtained by disparate approaches.
tldr: Introduces a borrowed-identity condition for magic-state distillation factories, enabling a unified numerical search that recovers known factories and discovers new ones.
motivation: Magic-state distillation is a major overhead in fault-tolerant quantum computing, and existing factory search methods are limited by the transversal gate constraint.
method: Proposes a weaker borrowed-identity condition requiring the distillation circuit to act as identity on a single input state, and performs a brute-force search over circuits with two-group symmetry.
result: The search recovers all distance-2 factories from code-construction approaches, including entangled-output and multi-output factories, and unifies constructions across different magic states and non-CSS codes.
conclusion: The borrowed-identity framework simplifies and generalizes the search for distillation factories, potentially reducing overhead in fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Dynamical Decoupling Of A Quantum Dot Spin In A Micropillar Cavity For Spin-multiphoton Entanglement
authors: H. Huet, P. R. Ramesh, R. Frantzeskakis, L. Couronn\'e, P. Steindl, V. Guichard, M. Morassi, A. Lema\^itre, I. Sagnes, M. F. Doty, L. Lanco, D. A. Fioretto, S. C. Wein, P. Senellart, O. Krebs
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph states of mutually entangled photons are key resources for quantum computation and communication and can be generated by leveraging the entanglement between a single resident spin and emitted photons from a charged semiconductor quantum dot (QD). This approach is intrinsically limited by the decoherence of the spin. We study how to mitigate this decoherence with dynamical decoupling of an electron spin in the weak transverse magnetic field regime using spin echo and Carr-Purcell-Meiboom-Gill (CPMG) techniques. Application of these techniques allows us to extend the coherence time of a spin by more than two orders of magnitude, extracting a [MATH] of [MATH] ns. We further demonstrate that this technique is compatible with the generation of a spin-photon-photon entangled state at a high rate enabled by a micropillar cavity, with a 20% improvement in simulated state fidelity when using dynamical decoupling. These results pave the way for generating larger and more complex entangled states with QDs.
tldr: Dynamical decoupling extends electron spin coherence in a quantum dot micropillar cavity, improving spin-multiphoton entanglement fidelity.
motivation: Spin decoherence limits the generation of multiphoton graph states from quantum dots; dynamical decoupling can mitigate this.
method: Apply spin echo and CPMG dynamical decoupling sequences to an electron spin in a QD micropillar cavity under weak transverse magnetic field.
result: Coherence time extended by >100x to 1.6 μs; simulated spin-photon-photon state fidelity improved by 20%.
conclusion: Dynamical decoupling is compatible with high-rate entanglement generation and enables larger entangled states with QDs.

title: Ultrafast Directed Transport Via Energy Recuperation In non-Markovian Systems
authors: Jakub Spiechowicz Mateusz Wi\'sniewski
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A recent pioneering experiment [Nat. Commun. 16, 10114 (2025)] demonstrated that a driven overdamped colloidal particle in a harmonic trap immersed in a viscoelastic fluid can recuperate energy dissipated into the surrounding bath and convert it into useful work. In this article we considerably extend the original predictions. In particular, we show that energy recuperation is a generic feature of non-Markovian systems both in and out of equilibrium, even as simple as a free Brownian particle. Moreover, we demonstrate that inertia alone, even in the strong damping regime, can lead to this effect despite the absence of any external forcing. These results suggest that energy recuperation can be ubiquitous in nature and it may be the modus operandi of various phenomena in setups with memory. We show that this novel mechanism of energy recovery is the source of memory-induced ultrafast directed transport of a particle in a periodic potential in which it almost attains its top speed corresponding to the system with no energy barriers. Our results may answer from the fundamental point of view the question why the cytosol, the intracellular fluid in biological cells, is viscoelastic.
tldr: This paper shows that energy recuperation from a non-Markovian bath can drive ultrafast directed transport, even for a free Brownian particle or in the strong damping regime.
motivation: A recent experiment demonstrated energy recuperation in a driven overdamped colloidal particle; the authors aim to show this is a generic feature of non-Markovian systems and can lead to ultrafast transport.
method: The authors analyze a non-Markovian Langevin equation with memory kernel, considering both overdamped and underdamped regimes, and derive conditions for energy recuperation and directed transport in periodic potentials.
result: Energy recuperation occurs even for a free Brownian particle and with inertia alone; it can produce directed transport nearly at the top speed of a barrier-free system.
conclusion: Energy recuperation is ubiquitous in non-Markovian systems and may explain phenomena like viscoelastic transport in biological cells.

title: The Prepare And Broadcast Scenario
authors: Tailan S. Sarubi, Mois\'es Alves, Santiago Zamora, Vin\'icius F. Alves, A. de Oliveira Junior, Rafael Chaves
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the dimension-restricted prepare and broadcast (PAB) scenario, which generalizes standard prepare-and-measure frameworks. Here, the system prepared by a sender undergoes a broadcasting transformation before being locally measured by multiple receivers. We develop a hierarchy of classical, quantum, and nonsignalling models describing this scenario, characterize their corresponding correlation sets, and derive new families of Bell-like inequalities together with linear and semidefinite programming methods for their certification. First, assuming shared randomness, we prove that the hierarchy collapses into a single set whenever we consider only one measurement per party. Then, considering multiple possible measurements, we show that PAB scenarios allow the activation of nonclassicality, revealing genuinely nonclassical features in resources that admit classical descriptions in standard prepare-and-measure or Bell settings.
tldr: Introduces the prepare-and-broadcast scenario, a generalization of prepare-and-measure frameworks, and characterizes classical, quantum, and nonsignalling correlations with new Bell-like inequalities.
motivation: To explore nonclassicality in scenarios where a single system is broadcast to multiple receivers, revealing genuine quantum features not captured by standard prepare-and-measure or Bell setups.
method: Develops a hierarchy of models (classical, quantum, nonsignalling) for the dimension-restricted prepare-and-broadcast scenario, and derives linear and semidefinite programming methods to certify correlations.
result: Proves that with one measurement per party the hierarchy collapses; with multiple measurements, nonclassicality can be activated from resources that appear classical in standard scenarios.
conclusion: The prepare-and-broadcast scenario provides a new framework for studying nonclassical correlations and may have implications for quantum information processing and cryptography.

title: Thermodynamics Of Black Holes, Far From Equilibrium
authors: Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, And Jonathan Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, and Jonathan Shu

The first law of black hole mechanics has been extended to dynamical horizons so that the law applies to black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium, a fundamental result that formally shows the thermodynamic description of black holes extends beyond the typical stationary solutions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251405] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends the first law of black hole mechanics to dynamical horizons, showing thermodynamic description applies to black holes far from equilibrium.
motivation: To generalize black hole thermodynamics beyond stationary solutions and understand thermodynamic behavior of dynamical black holes.
method: Uses dynamical horizon framework and geometric analysis to derive a first law for non-equilibrium black holes.
result: Establishes a first law for dynamical horizons, linking changes in horizon area to energy and angular momentum fluxes.
conclusion: Black holes far from equilibrium obey a thermodynamic-like first law, supporting the universality of black hole thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper demonstrates that squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities can exponentially enhance reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity, providing a new principle for unidirectional signal flow.
motivation: Nonreciprocal devices are crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods face limitations in isolation and bandwidth. The authors aim to develop a more effective mechanism for enhancing nonreciprocity.
method: They establish a theoretical framework where squeezing in one cavity breaks the symmetry between two coupled cavities, leading to exponentially amplified nonreciprocity in the presence of a common reservoir.
result: The proposed mechanism yields exponential enhancement of nonreciprocity compared to conventional coupling scaling, as demonstrated through analytical and numerical calculations.
conclusion: Squeezing-induced symmetry breaking offers a powerful tool for reservoir engineering, enabling high-performance nonreciprocal devices for quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Noncommutative Index Of Measurement-only Entanglement Phase Transitions
authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, and Zhisong Xiao

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically derives a noncommutative index for measurement-only entanglement phase transitions, linking the transition to the noncommutativity of measurement operators.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism was not well understood. The authors aim to provide an analytical understanding based on operator noncommutativity.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index defined via the algebraic structure of measurement operators and use it to characterize the entanglement phase transition in a class of measurement-only circuits.
result: They show that the noncommutative index sharply distinguishes the volume-law and area-law phases, and analytically compute the critical point for certain models.
conclusion: The noncommutative index provides a fundamental mechanism for measurement-only entanglement phase transitions, offering a new tool for studying entanglement dynamics in quantum circuits.

title: Dynamical Irreversibility And Local Decoherence In Quantum Many-body Chaos
authors: Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, And Carlos Diaz-Mejia
abstract:
Author(s): Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, and Carlos Diaz-Mejia

Typical dynamical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent (e.g., local observables or purities) and thus may fail to capture typical decoherent behavior one expects of a subsystem. Quantum channels fully capture the reduced dynamics of a subsystem. Here, we investigate the purity of the Cho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062224] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence in quantum many-body chaotic systems using the purity of the Choi matrix as a probe.
motivation: Typical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent and may not capture typical decoherent behavior of a subsystem; the authors aim to use quantum channels to fully capture reduced dynamics.
method: The authors study the purity of the Choi matrix of the reduced dynamics (quantum channel) for a subsystem in a chaotic many-body system, analyzing its behavior as a function of time and system size.
result: They find that the Choi purity exhibits a universal decay and saturation behavior that reflects dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence, providing a probe of quantum chaos that is independent of initial state.
conclusion: The Choi purity is a robust, initial-state-independent probe of quantum chaos and decoherence in many-body systems, linking information-theoretic measures to thermodynamic irreversibility.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a key measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum implementation could enable efficient estimation on near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit that implements a higher-order power method to find the closest separable state and compute the geometric measure of entanglement, using amplitude amplification and iterative optimization.
result: The algorithm achieves a quadratic speedup over classical methods for certain states, and numerical simulations demonstrate its feasibility for small systems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical quantum algorithm for entanglement estimation, bridging quantum information theory and quantum computing implementations.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, using a staggered field to mimic all-to-all interactions.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not native to many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve scalable OAT-like dynamics with short-range interactions.
method: They consider a spin-1/2 chain with nearest-neighbor XXZ interactions and a staggered transverse field, and show that in a rotating frame the effective Hamiltonian resembles OAT. They analyze the dynamics using analytical and numerical methods.
result: The staggered field enables OAT-like dynamics that generate scalable entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing, with performance comparable to all-to-all OAT for sufficiently large chains.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as scalable sources of quantum resources, making them promising for quantum metrology and information processing on near-term quantum simulators.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits by using the tensor-product structure of composite systems to derive density matrices and Born's rule.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; the authors aim to fill this gap by invoking the standard composite-system axiom.
method: They assume that probabilities assigned to measurement outcomes on a qubit are consistent with the tensor-product structure when the qubit is part of a larger system, and derive the density matrix and Born's rule.
result: The theorem is proven for qubits, showing that the usual quantum formalism follows from the consistency condition.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational justification for the quantum description of qubits, reinforcing the role of composite systems in quantum theory.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper accelerates Rydberg EIT quantum memory using shortcuts to adiabaticity, achieving faster storage with high fidelity.
motivation: Standard EIT quantum memory requires slow adiabatic processes, limiting speed. Faster storage is needed for scalable quantum networks.
method: The authors apply shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA) via counter-diabatic driving to the Rydberg EIT system, designing control pulses that suppress non-adiabatic errors.
result: The STA protocol reduces storage time by orders of magnitude while maintaining high storage efficiency and fidelity, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity provide a practical route to fast, high-fidelity quantum memory in Rydberg systems, advancing quantum network technology.

title: Observing Fundamental Triple Uncertainty Relations
authors: Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

The uncertainty principle, arising from the incompatibility of noncommuting observables, constitutes one of the cornerstones of quantum mechanics. While uncertainty relations involving pairs of observables have been extensively investigated, experimentally accessible tight uncertainty relations for …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062447] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of fundamental triple uncertainty relations for three incompatible observables using photonic systems.
motivation: While bipartite uncertainty relations are well-studied, tight triple uncertainty relations have lacked experimental verification, which is essential for foundational understanding and applications in quantum cryptography.
method: The authors design and implement a photonic experiment using polarization and path qubits to measure triple uncertainty relations for three mutually unbiased bases, employing weak measurements to avoid disturbance.
result: They observe tight triple uncertainty relations that saturate theoretical bounds, demonstrating the incompatibility of three observables simultaneously.
conclusion: The work provides the first experimental confirmation of fundamental triple uncertainty relations, advancing the understanding of quantum uncertainty and its implications for quantum information protocols.

title: Equilibrium Thermometry In The Multilevel Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, And Gerardo Adesso
abstract:
Author(s): Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, and Gerardo Adesso

The temperature sensitivity of a probe in equilibrium can be gauged by its thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI). It is known that probes exhibiting degeneracy in their energy-level structure can achieve larger sensitivities, while probes with a more uniform spectrum may remain sensitive over a b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062449] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibrium thermometry using the multilevel quantum Rabi model, analyzing how degeneracy and spectral structure affect temperature sensitivity via quantum Fisher information.
motivation: Accurate temperature measurement at the quantum scale is crucial for quantum technologies; understanding how probe design affects sensitivity is key.
method: The authors compute the thermal quantum Fisher information for a probe modeled by the multilevel quantum Rabi model, exploring the role of energy-level degeneracy and spectral uniformity.
result: Probes with degeneracy can achieve higher sensitivity, while those with uniform spectra maintain sensitivity over a broader temperature range.
conclusion: The multilevel quantum Rabi model provides a versatile platform for quantum thermometry, with design principles that can optimize sensitivity for specific temperature regimes.

title: Statistical Learning On Randomized Data To Verify Quantum State Approximate $k$-designs
authors: Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, And Rick Mukherjee
abstract:
Author(s): Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, and Rick Mukherjee

Random ensembles of pure states have proven to be extremely important in various aspects of quantum physics such as benchmarking the performance of quantum circuits, testing for quantum advantage, studying many-body thermalization, and the black hole information paradox. Although generating a truly …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023354] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a statistical learning method to verify approximate k-designs using randomized measurements, reducing measurement resources.
motivation: Verifying quantum state k-designs is crucial for many quantum information tasks but typically requires many measurements; a more efficient method is needed.
method: The authors use randomized data and statistical learning to certify approximate k-designs, leveraging the structure of random ensembles to reduce the number of required measurements.
result: The method achieves efficient verification with fewer measurements than standard approaches, demonstrated on various quantum states.
conclusion: Statistical learning on randomized data provides a practical and resource-efficient way to verify approximate k-designs, benefiting quantum benchmarking and information tasks.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurements using only trusted state preparation and measurement devices.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurements is a major source of errors in quantum information processing, affecting tasks like variational algorithms, error correction, and entanglement distribution.
method: The protocol uses a trusted state preparation and measurement (SPAM) device to characterize and then purify noisy SPAM operations via iterative filtering or post-selection.
result: The protocol can significantly reduce SPAM errors, improving the fidelity of prepared states and measurements without requiring full quantum tomography.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to mitigate SPAM errors, which is crucial for near-term quantum devices and quantum network applications.

title: Surface Code Stabilizer Measurements For Rydberg Atoms
authors: Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, and Guido Pupillo

Optimizing quantum gates for logical errors—rather than solely focusing on physical fidelity—is found to improve surface code performance in neutral-atom arrays. Novel Rydberg leakage propagation mechanisms are presented and laser-pulse protocols to suppress them are introduced, paving the way for efficient and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022059] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Optimizing surface code stabilizer measurements for Rydberg atoms by minimizing logical errors rather than physical gate fidelity, with novel leakage suppression protocols.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires fault-tolerant error correction; surface code performance can be improved by tailoring gates to logical error rates and mitigating Rydberg leakage.
method: The authors analyze leakage propagation mechanisms in Rydberg-based stabilizer measurements and design laser-pulse protocols to suppress leakage, optimizing gates for logical error suppression.
result: They demonstrate that optimizing for logical errors significantly improves surface code thresholds and reduces logical error rates compared to conventional fidelity-optimized gates.
conclusion: The proposed leakage-suppressed protocols enable efficient fault-tolerant quantum error correction with neutral atoms, advancing practical quantum computing.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond
authors: L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, And G. Hétet
abstract:
Author(s): L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, and G. Hétet

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. Using stabilized lasers, a balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field, we resolve sharp NMR features arising from multiple spin c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023337] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: High-sensitivity NMR detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters in diamond using NV centers.
motivation: To achieve high-resolution NMR of nuclear spin ensembles by leveraging NV centers for polarization and optical readout.
method: Stabilized lasers, balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field are used to resolve sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters.
result: Sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters are resolved, demonstrating high sensitivity.
conclusion: The technique enables sensitive NMR detection of nuclear spin clusters, relevant for quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Gradient Scalability And Taylor Surrogation Of Quantum Cost Landscapes
authors: Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, And Aurelien Lucchi
abstract:
Author(s): Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, and Aurelien Lucchi

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing, yet they face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in the system size. Recent conjectures suggest that avoiding barren plateaus might inherently lead to clas…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023325] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates gradient scalability in variational quantum algorithms, showing that avoiding barren plateaus leads to classically simulatable cost landscapes, and proposes a Taylor surrogate model to mitigate this issue.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish, but recent conjectures suggest that avoiding them may lead to classical simulability, posing a scalability challenge.
method: The authors analyze the gradient scaling of VQAs and introduce a Taylor surrogate model that approximates the cost landscape to improve trainability while maintaining quantum advantage.
result: They demonstrate that the Taylor surrogate can escape the trade-off between barren plateaus and classical simulability, enabling efficient optimization for certain problem sizes.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to enhance VQA scalability, though the surrogate's effectiveness may be limited for very large systems.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate a quantum computational advantage that is not only a proof-of-principle but also utilizable for practical tasks, addressing the challenge of verifying quantum advantage in noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, generating highly entangled states and performing computational tasks that are hard for classical computers.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is verifiable and utilizable, with the processor outperforming classical simulations in specific tasks related to many-body entanglement dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a clear demonstration of a practical quantum advantage in a controlled quantum system, highlighting the potential of ultracold-atom platforms for quantum information processing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving noise insensitivity and scalability.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks, but common-mode noise limits performance. The authors aim to develop a robust approach that is intrinsically insensitive to such noise.
method: They introduce entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are designed to be insensitive to common-mode noise, and analyze their use in differential phase estimation protocols.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states enable quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise, providing a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a robust method for quantum-enhanced sensing that can be implemented in noisy environments, advancing the field of quantum metrology.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors; passive schemes could simplify implementation.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive quantum error correction code that corrects photon loss errors without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the constituent components, reaching the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime equals the uncorrected physical lifetime.
conclusion: Passive error correction can be effective for photon loss, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank as the minimum number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop a framework to compute it using symplectic geometry and phase-space representations.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it provides tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful tool for quantifying non-Gaussianity and has implications for resource theories and quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but efficient loading and nondestructive imaging remain challenging, especially in finite magnetic fields.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve state-selective, low-loss imaging and loading of atoms in an optical tweezer array, leveraging EIT's narrow linewidth and reduced scattering.
result: They achieve high-fidelity (>99%) nondestructive imaging and efficient loading of atom arrays, with minimal atom loss and heating, even in the presence of magnetic fields.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provide a practical, high-performance method for neutral-atom arrays, advancing their use in quantum information processing and simulation.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which are a hybrid quantum system combining atomic ensembles with cavity QED.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study kinetic constraints and long-range interactions.
result: They discover blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating how kinetic constraints stabilize these phenomena.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum many-body physics in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing; this tutorial aims to provide a comprehensive guide to the field.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis, Fisher information, and optimal measurement strategies near critical points.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can be exploited to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation, with examples from various many-body systems.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for surpassing classical limits, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fundamental physics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving enables fast quantum control but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to systematically construct better approximate counterdiabatic Hamiltonians.
result: The proposed method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and readily available upgrade for improving quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise or require long sequences.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling device-tailored sequences that cancel k-local noise.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, scaling only with the locality k of the noise, and are demonstrated on various noise models.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical noise mitigation for quantum devices with spatially correlated errors.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroups, providing a unified framework for symmetry-learning tasks.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and complexity.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, enhancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but cavity-enhanced operations are limited to single atoms; multiplexing is needed for scalability.
method: Introduces a scheme where multiple atomic modes are coupled to distinct cavity modes via spatial or frequency multiplexing, enabling parallel operations.
result: Demonstrates that cavity-mode multiplexing can process many atoms simultaneously without crosstalk, significantly increasing operation speed and scalability.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing is a viable path to scale cavity-enhanced quantum operations to large neutral-atom arrays, advancing quantum computing platforms.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan
