method: The review compares regression-based methods, network-based architectures, and decomposition techniques for dynamical model discovery.
result: It evaluates strengths, limitations, and complementarity of these approaches, providing a guide for selecting appropriate methods.
conclusion: Data-driven discovery is a powerful tool for biological modeling, but careful method selection is crucial based on data characteristics and system complexity.

result: Radioactive molecules with octupole-deformed nuclei offer enhanced sensitivity to certain symmetry-violating effects, making them promising for fundamental physics tests.

tldr: This paper demonstrates all-optical control of spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskite materials via carrier-strain interaction, enhancing hot-carrier lifetime.

conclusion: The work provides insights into the physical mechanisms of cell protrusion formation, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

method: The authors develop a geometric reformulation of TDDFT, likely using concepts from differential geometry to better capture the dynamics of electronic systems out of equilibrium.

tldr: This paper develops a semiclassical theory for the orbital magnetic moment of Bogoliubov quasiparticles in superconductors.
motivation: Understanding the orbital magnetic moment of quasiparticles in superconductors is important for characterizing their response to magnetic fields.
method: The authors use a semiclassical wave-packet approach to derive the orbital magnetic moment from the energy correction linear in the magnetic field.
result: They obtain an expression for the orbital magnetic moment of Bogoliubov quasiparticles and apply it to a model superconductor.
conclusion: The semiclassical theory provides a framework to compute orbital magnetic moments in superconductors, which may be relevant for interpreting experiments.

title: Anyon Dispersion In Aharonov-Casher Bands And Implications For Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Zihan Yan, Qingchen Li, Tomohiro Soejima (副島智大), And Eslam Khalaf
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235155] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a microscopic theory of dispersing anyons in fractional quantum anomalous Hall systems, focusing on twisted MoTe2.
motivation: Understanding anyon dispersion is crucial for realizing itinerant anyon phases, but previous models assumed flat bands; this work accounts for realistic band geometry.
method: The authors construct momentum-resolved Laughlin quasihole states in Aharonov-Casher bands and use a momentum-space Monte Carlo framework to compute quasihole energies and bandwidths.
result: They find that nonuniform quantum geometry and the quasihole Berry phase lead to finite anyon dispersion, with bandwidths relevant to twisted MoTe2.
conclusion: The work provides a controlled route to study itinerant anyon phases and highlights the role of band geometry in anyon dynamics.

title: Magnetoexcitons And Massive Dirac Fermions In Monolayers Of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides In A High Magnetic Field
authors: Katarzyna Sadecka, Marek Korkusiński, Ludmiła Szulakowska, And Paweł Hawrylak

tldr: A theoretical study of magnetoexciton emission spectra in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides under high magnetic fields, focusing on interactions with quantum Hall states of massive Dirac fermions.
motivation: To understand the optical properties of TMD monolayers in strong magnetic fields, which is relevant for condensed matter physics but not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Uses an ab initio-parametrized massive Dirac fermion model including valley and spin degrees of freedom to compute the emission spectrum of magnetoexcitons interacting with quantum Hall states.
result: Provides a theoretical description of the emission spectrum, showing how magnetoexcitons couple to the quantum Hall state.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of excitonic and electronic properties in TMDs under high magnetic fields, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Anomalous Quasiparticle Lifetime In Geometric Quantum Critical Metals
authors: Hao Song, Han Ma, Catherine Kallin, And Sung-Sik Lee

tldr: This paper studies quasiparticle lifetime in metals undergoing geometric quantum phase transitions where Fermi surface curvature changes sign.
motivation: Understanding how geometric properties of the Fermi surface affect quasiparticle dynamics in quantum critical metals.
method: Theoretical analysis using field-theoretic methods to compute quasiparticle lifetime near inflection points on the Fermi surface.
result: Anomalous quasiparticle lifetime scaling due to vanishing local curvature at inflection points.
conclusion: Geometric quantum critical points lead to novel non-Fermi liquid behavior distinct from conventional quantum criticality.

title: Kondo Effect In Ferromagnetic Quantum Critical ${\mathrm{CeRh}}_{6}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{4}$
authors: Martin Sundermann, Joe D. Thompson, Eric D. Bauer, Chun-Fu Chang, Sheng-Huai Chen, Chang-Yang Kuo, Liu Hao Tjeng, Gertrud Zwicknagl, And Andrea Severing

tldr: This paper studies the Kondo effect and quantum criticality in a ferromagnetic heavy-fermion compound, focusing on cerium's 4f electron properties.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of pressure-induced quantum criticality in the heavy-fermion ferromagnet CeRh6Ge4 by investigating the nature of cerium's 4f electron.
method: Combining core-level photoemission and polarized x-ray absorption spectroscopy with simulations based on the single-impurity Anderson model.
result: Kondo hybridization admixes higher-lying crystal field states into a multiorbital ground state with 4f occupancy ~0.9, which also accounts for the dynamical spin response.
conclusion: Kondo hybridization and the resulting multiorbital ground state are essential components for a model of quantum criticality in this system.

tldr: This paper studies the Yamaji effect in underdoped cuprates, focusing on magnetoresistance and hole pocket geometry.
motivation: To explain recent angle-dependent magnetoresistance measurements in underdoped cuprates that show evidence of small hole pockets in the pseudogap regime.
method: The authors use theoretical models of underdoped cuprates to analyze the Yamaji effect and compare with experimental data.
result: The analysis reproduces the observed Yamaji effect, confirming the presence of hole pockets and providing insights into the pseudogap phase.
conclusion: The study supports the existence of small hole pockets in underdoped cuprates and advances understanding of the pseudogap regime.

title: Revisiting The Origin Of The Stokes Shift By Bridging Absorption And Emission Through The Optoelectronic Reciprocity Relation
authors: Meita Asami, Kentaroh Watanabe, And Masakazu Sugiyama
abstract:

In this study, we investigate the interpretation of the Stokes shift (SS) by employing the optoelectronic reciprocity relation (ORR), which provides a fundamental link between optical absorption and emission processes. tldr: This paper uses the optoelectronic reciprocity relation to reinterpret the Stokes shift in semiconductor materials.
motivation: To provide a fundamental understanding of the Stokes shift by linking absorption and emission processes through the optoelectronic reciprocity relation.
method: The authors revisit the van Roosbroeck-Shockley relation and generalized Planck's law, applying the optoelectronic reciprocity relation to bridge absorption and emission.
result: They derive a new interpretation of the Stokes shift based on the reciprocity relation.
conclusion: The optoelectronic reciprocity relation offers a unified framework for understanding the Stokes shift in semiconductors.

title: Screened Potential In One-dimensional Systems: Application To Electron-hole Interaction And Wannier-Mott-like Excitons In Atomic Wires
authors: F. Bechstedt, S. Grillo, O. Pulci, And P. Gori
abstract:

The geometry and electronic properties of nanostructures such as chains, wires, and ribbons, which are restricted in two dimensions, give rise to novel and unexpected physical phenomena. We derive the screened Coulomb potential in one-dimensional (1D) systems by solving the Poisson equation for diff…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245432] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the screened Coulomb potential in one-dimensional systems and applies it to electron-hole interactions and excitons in atomic wires.
motivation: Understanding the screened Coulomb potential in 1D systems is crucial for predicting excitonic effects in nanostructures like atomic wires.
method: The authors solve the Poisson equation for a dielectric environment to obtain the screened potential, then use it to model electron-hole interactions.
result: They find that the screened potential leads to bound exciton states with binding energies significantly larger than in bulk materials.
conclusion: The derived potential provides a foundation for studying excitons and many-body effects in quasi-1D systems.

title: Many-body Wave Function And Edge Magnetization Of An Open $p+is$ Superconducting Chain
authors: Jiarui Jiao, Chao Xu, Congjun Wu, And Wang Yang
abstract:

Although BCS wave functions for superconductors under periodic boundary conditions are well established, obtaining an explicit form of the many-body BCS wave function under open boundary condition is usually a nontrivial problem. In this work, we construct the exact BCS ground-state wave function of…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224525] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs the exact BCS ground-state wave function for a p+is superconducting chain under open boundary conditions and studies its edge magnetization.
motivation: BCS wave functions under periodic boundary conditions are well known, but obtaining explicit forms under open boundary conditions is nontrivial and important for understanding edge properties.
method: The authors analytically construct the many-body BCS wave function for an open p+is superconducting chain using a Bogoliubov transformation and solve for the edge magnetization.
result: They obtain an exact expression for the ground-state wave function and compute the edge magnetization, revealing nontrivial edge physics.
conclusion: The work provides a rare exact solution for a superconducting system with open boundaries, highlighting edge effects in topological superconductors.

title: Flat-band Driven Kondo Breakdown And Reentrant Effects In Heavy-fermion Moiré Superlattices
authors: Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, And Benedikt Fauseweh

tldr: This paper studies Kondo breakdown and reentrant effects in heavy-fermion moiré superlattices, focusing on strongly correlated electronic phenomena.
motivation: Moiré superlattices in van der Waals heterostructures can host emergent electronic phenomena similar to bulk strongly correlated materials, motivating the study of heavy-fermion physics in these systems.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical methods to analyze the Kondo lattice model in moiré superlattices, exploring flat-band effects on Kondo screening.
result: They find that flat bands can drive a Kondo breakdown and lead to reentrant heavy-fermion behavior under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work reveals new aspects of heavy-fermion physics in moiré systems, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

tldr: This paper shows that orbital magnetization responses can reveal multiband topological invariants in electronic systems.
motivation: To find a way to probe nontrivial multiband topology through measurable physical quantities.
method: Decomposing orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions and analyzing its response to external magnetic fields.
result: The decomposition allows deduction of multiband topological invariants from orbital magnetization.
conclusion: Orbital magnetization is a useful probe for multiband topology, linking quantum geometry to observable responses.

title: Large Anomalous Hall Conductivity And Topological Hall Effect In The Kagome Helimagnet ${\mathrm{MgMn}}_{6}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{6}$

motivation: To explore exotic topological transport phenomena in magnetic kagome materials, which are a platform for studying Berry-curvature-driven effects.
method: Synthesis of MgMn6Ge6 single crystals, measurement of Hall conductivity and magnetization, and analysis using Berry-curvature concepts.
result: Large anomalous Hall conductivity and topological Hall effect are observed, linked to the non-trivial spin texture of the kagome lattice.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of Berry curvature in kagome helimagnets and suggest potential for spintronic applications.

title: Strain-driven Antiferroelastic Switching Of Altermagnetism

tldr: This paper demonstrates nonvolatile control of altermagnetic spin states via antiferroelastic lattice distortion.
motivation: Nonvolatile control of altermagnetism is crucial for spintronic device applications, but remains a key challenge.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to show that antiferroelastic distortion can switch the altermagnetic order parameter.
result: They find that strain-driven antiferroelastic switching enables reversible and nonvolatile control of spin splitting.
conclusion: This work provides a mechanism for electrically or mechanically controlling altermagnetic states, advancing spintronics.

method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on the momentum-dependent anisotropic spin splitting in the altermagnet band structure to compute spin-transfer torque and its effect on the Néel vector.
result: They find that the asymmetric effective exchange fields on the two sublattices can induce deterministic Néel vector switching via spin-transfer torque.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for using spin-transfer torque to control altermagnetic order, which may enable new spintronic devices.

motivation: Understanding interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions is important for nanoelectronics, but the work does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors perform theoretical analysis using tight-binding or DFT calculations to predict interface states for various width combinations and geometries.
result: They find that predicting the number of interface states requires considerations beyond simple width matching.
conclusion: The study provides guidelines for engineering interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions, but has no relevance to the specified research directions.

result: The theory successfully explains known unconventional magnetic behaviors and predicts new ones in various bilayer systems.
conclusion: The stacking theory provides a systematic approach to engineer magnetism in bilayer 2D materials, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

method: Density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) with spiral boundary conditions to map finite clusters onto one-dimensional chains.

method: The authors implement AFQMC in VASP using plane-wave basis and PAW formalism, with exact inversion of the PAW overlap operator to maintain cubic scaling.

conclusion: The AFQMC implementation in VASP provides a practical and accurate tool for computing lattice constants and other ground-state properties of solids.

title: Orbital Hybridization Induces Giant Cubic Rashba Effect At The $\text{Cu/}{\mathrm{WO}}_{3}$ Interface

method: First-principles density functional theory calculations are performed on the Cu/WO3 heterostructure to analyze the electronic structure and Rashba splitting.
result: A giant cubic Rashba effect is observed, attributed to orbital hybridization between Cu and WO3, with a large Rashba coefficient.
conclusion: Orbital hybridization at oxide interfaces can produce strong Rashba effects, offering a new route for spintronic materials without heavy elements.

title: Exceptional Rings Emerging In A non-Hermitian Rice-Mele Ladder

result: They identify a crossover in the ordered phase that depends on the interaction range exponent, revealing new features beyond the Mermin-Wagner-Hohenberg theorem.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the phase diagram of long-range spin systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics as defined in the research interests.

result: Quorum sensing promotes antifragile regimes that increase bacterial community diversity.

tldr: This paper presents a high-stability optical clock based on a continuously ground-state cooled Al+ ion, achieving reduced averaging time without compromising accuracy.
motivation: Single-ion optical clocks have high systematic accuracy but require long averaging times to reach statistical uncertainty; this work aims to reduce that time without sacrificing accuracy.
method: The authors implement continuous ground-state cooling of an Al+ ion to enable longer probe times while mitigating time-dilation shifts, and characterize the clock's stability and accuracy.
result: The clock achieves a fractional frequency instability below 10^-15 at 1 second and a systematic uncertainty at the 10^-18 level, with significantly reduced averaging time compared to previous single-ion clocks.
conclusion: Continuous ground-state cooling allows single-ion optical clocks to combine high accuracy with high stability, making them more practical for precision timekeeping applications.

title: One-particle Density Matrix Framework For Mode-shell Correspondence: Characterizing Topology In Amorphous Higher-order Topological Insulators
authors: Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, And Julia D. Hannukainen
abstract:
Author(s): Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, and Julia D. Hannukainen

We present a framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases directly from the one-particle density matrix, without any reference to an underlying Hamiltonian. Our approach extends the mode-shell correspondence, originally formulated for single-particle Hamiltonians, to Gaussian states …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases in amorphous systems using the one-particle density matrix.
motivation: To extend the mode-shell correspondence to Gaussian states and characterize topology in amorphous higher-order topological insulators without a Hamiltonian.
method: Develops a one-particle density matrix framework that generalizes the mode-shell correspondence to Gaussian states, enabling topological characterization from the density matrix alone.
result: The framework successfully identifies topological phases in amorphous higher-order topological insulators, demonstrating the mode-shell correspondence in a broader context.
conclusion: The one-particle density matrix provides a robust tool for topological characterization in disordered systems, extending the applicability of the mode-shell correspondence.

title: Ligand-mediated Magnetic Coupling Across Metamagnetic Transitions In ${\mathrm{CrPS}}_{4}$
authors: Giuseppe Buccoliero, Rachel Nickel, Roberto Sant, Marli Dos Reis Cantarino, Andrei Rogalev, Nathan J. Yutronkie, Tristan Riccardi, Daniel A. Chaney, Kurt Kummer, Johann Coraux, And Nicholas B. Brookes
abstract:
Author(s): Giuseppe Buccoliero, Rachel Nickel, Roberto Sant, Marli dos Reis Cantarino, Andrei Rogalev, Nathan J. Yutronkie, Tristan Riccardi, Daniel A. Chaney, Kurt Kummer, Johann Coraux, and Nicholas B. Brookes

Chromium thiophosphate ([MATH]) is a long-known material: A layered semiconducting antiferromagnet. Its recently discovered gate-tunable metamagnetic phase transitions, the remarkable positive and oscillating magnetoresistance as a tunnel barrier, and its Fano-resonance luminescence, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023323] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates ligand-mediated magnetic coupling and metamagnetic transitions in CrPS4, a layered semiconducting antiferromagnet.
motivation: Understanding the magnetic properties of CrPS4 is important for potential applications in spintronics and magnetoelectronics.
method: The authors use X-ray absorption spectroscopy and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism to probe the electronic and magnetic structure across metamagnetic transitions.
result: They find that ligand-mediated superexchange interactions play a key role in the magnetic coupling, and the metamagnetic transitions are accompanied by changes in the ligand field.
conclusion: The study provides insight into the microscopic mechanism of metamagnetism in CrPS4, which may guide future material design.

title: Excited Eigenstates From A Two-species Random Walk
authors: Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, And Alexandre Melanson
abstract:
Author(s): Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, and Alexandre Melanson

Macroscopically, the population density function of random walk models can satisfy self-contained dynamics and exhibit unexpected order. Here, we show how a two-species random walk model that includes diffusion, probabilistic absorption of walkers mediated by a potential function, cross-species anni…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023324] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A two-species random walk model with diffusion, absorption, and cross-species annihilation is studied, showing emergent order in population density.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic order can arise from simple stochastic microscopic rules in multi-species systems.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a two-species random walk with diffusion, probabilistic absorption, and cross-species annihilation.
result: The population density function satisfies self-contained dynamics and exhibits unexpected order.
conclusion: The model demonstrates emergent order in a stochastic system, relevant to pattern formation and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Theory Of High-harmonic Generation With Quantum Light
authors: Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, And Jianmin Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, and Jianmin Yuan

High-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by intense quantum light has recently emerged as a new frontier in strong-field physics. Yet, the mechanism underlying HHG with nonclassical fields such as bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) light—characterized by a vanishing mean electric field—remains elusive. In th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023326] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of high-harmonic generation driven by quantum light, specifically bright squeezed vacuum, using a quantum-optical framework.
motivation: High-harmonic generation with nonclassical light is a new frontier, but the mechanism for bright squeezed vacuum with zero mean field is not understood.
method: The authors employ a quantum-optical approach treating both the driving field and the atomic system quantum mechanically, deriving an effective Hamiltonian and solving the dynamics.
result: They show that HHG can occur even with zero mean field due to quantum fluctuations, and predict distinct features in the harmonic spectrum compared to classical driving.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for HHG with quantum light, opening up new possibilities for strong-field physics and attosecond science.

title: Contrasting Impurity-induced Magnetism And Dynamics In $2H\text{−}{\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Jonas A. Krieger, Igor P. Rusinov, Sourabh Barua, Aris Chatzichristos, Jared Croese, Derek Fujimoto, Stefan Holenstein, Victoria L. Karner, Ryan M. L. Mcfadden, John O. Ticknor, W. Andrew Macfarlane, Robert F. Kiefl, Geetha Balakrishnan, Evgueni V. Chulkov, Stuart S. P. Parkin, And Zaher Salman

Andrew MacFarlane, Robert F. Kiefl, Geetha Balakrishnan, Evgueni V. Chulkov, Stuart S. P. Parkin, and Zaher Salman

We investigate the behavior of interstitial [MATH] implanted near the surface of [MATH] using [MATH]-detected nuclear magnetic resonance. We find that, unlike the muon, [MATH] does not show any signature of induced magnetism. This result is consist…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023316] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies impurity-induced magnetism and dynamics in 2H-MoTe2 using beta-detected NMR, focusing on material properties rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the behavior of interstitial Li implanted near the surface of 2H-MoTe2 and compare with muon behavior.
method: Beta-detected nuclear magnetic resonance (β-NMR) was used to probe Li implantation and dynamics.
result: Unlike muons, Li does not show any signature of induced magnetism; the results are consistent with no magnetic ordering.
conclusion: The study provides insights into impurity-induced magnetism in this material, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Tunable Intertwining Via Collective Excitations
authors: András Szabó And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): András Szabó and R. Chitra

Periodically driven collective excitations emerging when two distinct symmetry-broken phases give rise to a manifold of enlarged symmetry are explored. The work proposes that the resulting driven phase diagram hosting out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases is accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experimental setups.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022053] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies periodically driven collective excitations in symmetry-broken phases leading to out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases, accessible in matter-cavity setups.
motivation: To explore driven phases of matter where collective excitations from distinct symmetry-broken phases intertwine, potentially revealing new non-equilibrium phenomena.
method: Theoretical analysis of periodically driven collective excitations emerging from a manifold of enlarged symmetry, with a proposed phase diagram.
result: A driven phase diagram hosting out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases is proposed, accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experimental setups.
conclusion: The work suggests that such intertwined phases can be realized experimentally, offering a platform to study non-equilibrium physics.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses simulations to study relaxation dynamics in deeply supercooled liquids, focusing on rare cage escapes.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in glass-forming liquids is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare events.
result: The study identifies that rare cage escapes are the primary drivers of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems, but the work is purely in condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experimental demonstrations.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations operate in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, leaving a theoretical gap.
method: The authors develop new complexity-theoretic arguments and hardness proofs tailored to the saturated regime of BosonSampling with linear mode counts.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in this regime remains classically hard under plausible conjectures, providing theoretical support for current experiments.
conclusion: The work validates the quantum advantage claims of near-term photonic experiments by extending the theoretical foundation to experimentally relevant parameter regimes.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of quantum chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
motivation: To understand the quantum behavior of chiral solitons in spin chains and their experimental signatures.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons in spin chains.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: These solitons are detectable via inelastic neutron scattering, providing a way to observe quantum soliton dynamics.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative regularization, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs numerically.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute critical exponents and operator dimensions.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying fermionic CFTs, and emergent supersymmetry may be a generic feature of such theories.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin textures in moiré superstructures is important for manipulating information via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based information manipulation.
conclusion: The work provides a general approach to engineering spin moiré superstructures for potential applications in information processing.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie point.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for engineering robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To develop a general method for predicting physical links in networks based on observed dynamics.
method: The authors propose a physics-informed framework that leverages dynamical equations to infer causal interactions.
result: The framework successfully infers causal links across a range of networked dynamical systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a general tool for network inference with potential applications in various fields.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
