title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory for stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for astrophysics, but direct measurements are often impossible due to extremely low cross sections.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques to study these reactions.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical models and experimental methods for low-energy nuclear reactions in stars.
conclusion: The review highlights the need for continued theoretical and experimental efforts to better understand stellar nucleosynthesis and energy generation.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, and periodic updates incorporate new measurements and improved uncertainties.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, taking into account correlations and uncertainties.
result: A self-consistent set of values for the fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, with updated uncertainties.
conclusion: The 2022 CODATA values supersede previous sets and serve as the internationally recommended reference for fundamental constants.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser-induced ultrasound to image biological tissues.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy can image millimeters to centimeters deep with high resolution, providing optical contrast in biological tissues.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing advancements in multimodal approaches.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory for buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with applications in materials science and biology.
motivation: Understanding the formation of creases and cusps during buckling of soft materials is important for morphogenesis and swelling of gels.
method: The review integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, including bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and elliptic integrals.
result: It provides a modern treatment of the Biot instability and explains how nonlinear elasticity captures crease and cusp formation.
conclusion: Nonlinear elasticity theory is essential for a complete understanding of buckling patterns in soft matter.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses gravitational wave signals from the early universe, including phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: Gravitational waves offer a unique probe of the first second of the universe, as they are not blocked by the primordial plasma.
method: The paper reviews theoretical predictions for stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds from cosmological sources and detection strategies.
result: It summarizes potential signals from phase transitions, topological defects, and other early-universe phenomena.
conclusion: Gravitational waves can reveal information about the earliest moments of the universe, complementing electromagnetic and neutrino observations.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools for constructing and using Wannier functions in condensed-matter physics.
method: The paper surveys the ecosystem of software packages that implement Wannier-function approaches, describing their capabilities and interoperability.
result: The review catalogs the major software tools and their applications, highlighting the widespread use of Wannier functions in electronic structure calculations.
conclusion: The Wannier-function software ecosystem is a major instrument for understanding and designing materials, with broad applications in condensed-matter physics.

title: Causality Of Ultrafast Photoionization From Argon 3 S Usin...
authors: Rezvan Tahouri And Jan Marcus Dahlström
abstract: We study real-time photoionization flux at the Amusia–Cooper minimum (ACM) in argon using ab initio simulations with the relativistic time-dependent configuration-interaction singles (RTDCIS) method in length (LG) and velocity (VG) gauges. A simple analytical model is used to interpret the results, and to construct Wigner delays and Wigner distributions for both gauges and relativistic channels of the photoelectron ( with and ). The two gauges are found to produce qualitatively different ionization dynamics, with LG having positive and VG having negative Wigner delays. The advancement of several femtoseconds, found for Wigner delays in VG, raises some concern for causality when atoms are ionized by attosecond pulses that are shorter than the absolute value of the Wigner delay. Reassuringly, numerical simulations of wave packets with RTDCIS show that the electrons behave in a causal way in both gauges. Weighted delays that take into account the temporal window of excitation (or the bandwidth of the pulses) are constructed from the Wigner distribution to reach agreement between the numerical simulations and our simple wave packet model. Furthermore, a strong effect of spin–orbit coupling of the photoelectron ( ) is reported for ultrafast photoionization dynamics, and Schrödinger kitten and cat states are identified in the Wigner distributions as a result of the ACM. Our work paves the way for a deeper understanding of ultrafast photoionization and the role of causality in systems with strong electron–electron correlation effects.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast photoionization dynamics in argon, focusing on causality and Wigner delays at the Amusia-Cooper minimum.
motivation: To understand the role of causality in ultrafast photoionization and resolve gauge-dependent discrepancies in Wigner delays.
method: Ab initio simulations using relativistic time-dependent configuration-interaction singles (RTDCIS) in length and velocity gauges, combined with a simple analytical model.
result: Length and velocity gauges yield qualitatively different ionization dynamics; velocity gauge shows negative Wigner delays raising causality concerns, but full wave-packet simulations confirm causal behavior.
conclusion: Weighted delays constructed from Wigner distributions reconcile gauge differences, and spin-orbit coupling effects are significant; Schrödinger kitten/cat states are identified.

motivation: Understanding the role of voltage in tuning chemical properties of self-assembled monolayers on electrodes is important for designing electrochemical systems.

result: The new theoretical framework captures the influence of applied voltage on molecular properties and reaction barriers at electrochemical interfaces.
conclusion: Fractional charge DFT provides a useful tool for predicting and designing voltage-controlled chemical processes at electrodes.

title: Ai Agents Are Sensitive To Nudges
authors: Manuel Chereppattie Maesnikhil Singhahttps://ror.org/042nb2s44media Lab, Massachusetts Institute Of Technology, Cambridge, MA 02139bhttps://ror.org/049s0rh22department Of Computer Science, Dartmouth College, Hanover, NH 03755

motivation: To test the assumption that AI agents behave rationally or human-like under uncertainty.
method: The authors design a benchmark based on human choice strategies and evaluate AI agents' sensitivity to nudges.

title: Direct Demonstration Of Electric Chirality Control In A Helimagnetic YMn6Sn6 By Spin-polarized Neutron Scattering
authors: Hidetoshi Masudayutaro Yanagisawakazuki Ohishiyusuke Nambuyoichi Niiyoshinori Onoseahttps://ror.org/01dq60k83institute For Materials Research, Tohoku University, Sendai 980-8577, Miyagi, Japanbhttps://ror.org/03gb41d27neutron Science And Technology Center, Comprehensive Research Organization For Science And Society (CROSS), Tokai 319-1106, Ibaraki, Japanchttps://ror.org/02kpeqv85institute For Integrated Radiation And Nuclear Science, Kyoto University, Kumatori 590-0494, Osaka, Japandhttps://ror.org/02kn6nx58department Of Applied Physics And Physico-Informatics, Keio University, Yokohama 223-8522, Kanagawa, Japanehttps://ror.org/01dq60k83center For Science And Innovation In Spintronics (CSIS), Tohoku University, Sendai 980-8577, Miyagi, Japan

tldr: This paper demonstrates electric chirality control in a helimagnetic material using spin-polarized neutron scattering.
motivation: Chirality in helimagnets offers a platform for information encoding, but direct electric control of magnetic chirality has not been shown.
method: The authors use spin-polarized neutron scattering to observe the magnetic structure of YMn6Sn6 under applied electric fields.
result: They demonstrate that the magnetic chirality can be switched by an electric field, showing direct electric control.
conclusion: Electric chirality control in helimagnets is feasible, which may enable new spintronic devices.

title: The Optics Of Shadow Bands
authors: Branko Sretenovi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shadow bands are transient, rippling patterns of light and dark that may appear in moments before and after totality in a solar eclipse. Despite centuries of reports, their physical origin has remained unresolved. This preprint develops a geometric-optical solution in which the Sun's extended structure produces a celestial analogue of Young's double-slit experiment, generating an interference-like intensity pattern on the ground, modulated by Earth-atmosphere effects. The analysis combines solar limb geometry, atmospheric propagation effects, and a wave-based formulation that yields quantitative predictions for fringe width and spacing. The resulting model accounts for the principal observational features of shadow bands and clarifies why the phenomenon is both elusive and highly sensitive to viewing conditions.
tldr: This paper proposes a geometric-optical model for shadow bands observed during solar eclipses, attributing them to interference-like patterns from the Sun's extended structure.
motivation: Shadow bands have been observed for centuries but their physical origin remained unresolved; this work aims to provide a quantitative explanation.
method: The author develops a wave-based formulation combining solar limb geometry and atmospheric propagation effects to model the intensity pattern on the ground.
result: The model yields quantitative predictions for fringe width and spacing, accounting for the principal observational features of shadow bands.
conclusion: The phenomenon is explained as a celestial analogue of Young's double-slit experiment, modulated by Earth-atmosphere effects, clarifying its elusive nature.

title: Signs And Signatures Of Intelligence
authors: Julia Demarines
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Research into the emergence and evolution of intelligence is underrepresented in astrobiology. I propose noosemiotics, the study of noosignatures, to address this gap. Noosignatures are the structured traces that minds leave on a medium, whether physical (tools, etchings, architecture) or signal-based (encoded transmissions, complex animal communication), that remain detectable as the products of intelligence regardless of whether their meaning can be recovered. Where biosignatures mark life and technosignatures mark technology, noosignatures mark the space between. This paper defines noosemiotics, situates it within astrobiology, and proposes a research program for empirical metrics, with material culture as the primary test bed.
tldr: This paper proposes a new field called noosemiotics to study traces of intelligence (noosignatures) in astrobiology, bridging biosignatures and technosignatures.
motivation: Research into the emergence and evolution of intelligence is underrepresented in astrobiology; the paper aims to fill this gap by defining a framework for detecting signs of intelligence.
method: The paper defines noosemiotics and noosignatures, situates them within astrobiology, and proposes a research program for empirical metrics using material culture as a test bed.
result: No empirical results are presented; the paper is a conceptual proposal outlining a new research direction.
conclusion: Noosemiotics could provide a systematic way to study intelligence in astrobiology, but the paper does not advance quantum information theory or related fields.

title: The Heat-kernel Master Field On $\mathbb{Z}^d$ At Strong Coupling
authors: Thibaut Lemoine
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve large-[MATH] Yang--Mills theory on [MATH], for every [MATH], at strong coupling, for structure group [MATH] and for the heat-kernel action. More precisely, we prove that normalized Wilson loop expectations have infinite-volume large-[MATH] limits, factorize at leading order, and admit an all-order [MATH]-expansion with exponentially local coefficients, whose leading order characterizes the master field. We also prove an area-law upper bound for the heat-kernel master field, with a stronger coefficientwise version. The proof is based on a rooted heat-kernel master loop equation. Unlike the Wilson-action equation or the two-dimensional Makeenko--Migdal equation, this equation does not close on Wilson loop observables alone; it closes on an extended space of loop observables coupled to compactly supported plaquette decorations. We prove a strong-coupling, order-truncated rooted trajectory expansion and then identify its leading term with the master field. The main inputs are the universal finite-[MATH] duality formulas developed in the companion paper and large-[MATH] heat-kernel estimates from .
tldr: This paper solves large-N Yang-Mills theory on Z^d at strong coupling with heat-kernel action, proving factorization and area-law bounds for Wilson loop expectations.
motivation: To understand the master field in large-N Yang-Mills theory, which is a key problem in quantum field theory and mathematical physics.
method: Uses a rooted heat-kernel master loop equation and a strong-coupling, order-truncated rooted trajectory expansion, combined with finite-N duality formulas and large-N heat-kernel estimates.
result: Proves that normalized Wilson loop expectations have infinite-volume large-N limits, factorize at leading order, and admit an all-order 1/N-expansion with exponentially local coefficients; also proves an area-law upper bound for the heat-kernel master field.
conclusion: The heat-kernel master field on Z^d is solved at strong coupling, providing a rigorous foundation for the master field and area law in this regime.

title: On Apostol-Type Mersenne-Bernoulli And Mersenne-Euler Polynomials
authors: Prasanta Kumar Ray Artatrana Suna
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the Apostol-type Mersenne-Bernoulli and Mersenne-Euler polynomials of order [MATH]. By employing the [MATH]-calculus, based on the Mersenne numbers, we establish explicit series representations, addition theorems, difference equations and convolution identities.
tldr: This paper introduces Apostol-type Mersenne-Bernoulli and Mersenne-Euler polynomials using q-calculus based on Mersenne numbers.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the theory of special polynomials by incorporating Mersenne numbers into Apostol-type polynomials.
method: They employ q-calculus and Mersenne numbers to define new polynomial sequences and derive explicit series representations, addition theorems, difference equations, and convolution identities.
result: New families of polynomials are introduced with various algebraic properties established.
conclusion: The work contributes to the combinatorial theory of special functions but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Telstar Balls Gone Wild
authors: Thomas Fernique
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe an artistic project consisting of fabricating the 3532 different soccer balls that can be obtained by randomly assembling the 32 pieces of a classic Telstar soccer ball.
tldr: This paper describes an artistic project to fabricate all possible random assemblies of a classic Telstar soccer ball.
motivation: The motivation is artistic exploration of combinatorial soccer ball designs.
method: The method involves randomly assembling the 32 pieces of a Telstar soccer ball to generate 3532 distinct balls.
result: The result is the fabrication of all 3532 different soccer balls.
conclusion: The paper concludes with a description of the artistic project and its outcomes.

title: Equilibria In Motion: Stability, Tracking, And Convergence
authors: Hassan Saoud
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stability, tracking, and convergence of nonautonomous systems with time-varying nonisolated equilibrium sets. A Lyapunov framework based on coupled dissipation channels is developed to analyze the evolution of trajectories relative to a moving equilibrium family whose variation is quantified by an equilibrium speed measured through local Hausdorff estimates. Under suitable dissipation and energy--distance comparison conditions, we establish Lyapunov stability, quantitative tracking bounds, asymptotic tracking under integrable equilibrium drift, and an input-to-state stability estimate relative to the moving equilibrium family. We further show that integrable equilibrium speed implies the existence of a limiting equilibrium geometry obtained through local Hausdorff convergence of the equilibrium sets and that convergence to the moving equilibrium family can be transferred to convergence relative to the limiting equilibrium set. Quantitative convergence estimates are also derived. The theory is illustrated by a dynamic resource allocation model with time-varying demand.
tldr: This paper develops a Lyapunov framework for stability and tracking of nonautonomous systems with time-varying equilibrium sets, applied to resource allocation.
motivation: To analyze systems where equilibrium sets move over time, which is common in dynamic environments.
method: Uses coupled dissipation channels and local Hausdorff estimates to quantify equilibrium speed and derive Lyapunov stability, tracking bounds, and convergence.
result: Establishes Lyapunov stability, quantitative tracking bounds, asymptotic tracking under integrable drift, and input-to-state stability relative to moving equilibrium families.
conclusion: The framework provides a rigorous way to handle time-varying equilibria, with convergence to a limiting equilibrium set under integrable drift.

title: Stability Refinements Of The Triangle Inequality In $L^p$ Spaces
authors: Ruizhou Song
abstract:
ArXiv:2606.28435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a measure space and let [MATH]. We study quantitative stability refinements of Minkowski's inequality \[ \| f + g\|_{p}\leq \| f\|_{p} + \| g\|_{p} \] for real-valued functions in \(L^p(X,\mu)\). We first establish a stability estimate for arbitrary real-valued functions and show that its constant is sharp. We then prove that, for nonnegative functions, the constant can be improved when \(p\geq 2\), again to its optimal value. More precisely, if \(f,g\geq 0\) and \(f,g\neq 0\), then \[ \| f + g\|_{p}\leq \| f\|_{p} + \| g\|_{p} - c_{p}\min \{\| f\|_{p},\| g\|_{p}\} \left\| {\| f\|_{p}} -{\| g\|_{p}}\right\|_{p}^{\alpha_{p}}, \] where \[ c_p = {4}, & 1

tldr: This paper proves sharp stability refinements of Minkowski's inequality in L^p spaces.
motivation: To obtain quantitative stability versions of the triangle inequality for L^p functions, with optimal constants.
method: The authors derive stability estimates for arbitrary real-valued functions and then improve the constant for nonnegative functions when p≥2, using analytic inequalities.
result: They establish sharp constants c_p and exponents α_p for the stability refinement, showing both are best possible.
conclusion: The work provides optimal stability refinements of Minkowski's inequality, contributing to functional analysis but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A New $L2-1_{\sigma}$-Interior Penalty Method For Variable-Order Time-Fractional Subdiffusion Interface Problem With Curved Interface
authors: Hongying Huang, Chanchan Hao, Changmu Yu, Huili Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper treats variable-order time-fractional subdiffusion with discontinuous coefficients across a curved interface using [MATH] time stepping on graded meshes and a symmetric interior penalty FEM on body-fitted meshes. Stability and optimal a priori error estimates in a discrete-in-time [MATH] norm are established, yielding second-order temporal accuracy. While analysis typically assumes [MATH] at [MATH] lies in the range of [MATH] on [MATH] and [MATH], experiments indicate the second inequality can be relaxed or omitted, enabling straightforward selection of [MATH] from many admissible values without solving a nonlinear equation. Numerical results verify temporal rates [MATH], spatial order [MATH], and robustness to superconvergent points and interface geometry.
tldr: This paper develops a numerical method for solving variable-order time-fractional subdiffusion interface problems with curved interfaces.
motivation: To accurately solve subdiffusion problems with discontinuous coefficients across curved interfaces, which arise in various physical applications.
method: It uses L2-1_sigma time stepping on graded meshes and a symmetric interior penalty finite element method on body-fitted meshes.
result: Second-order temporal accuracy and optimal spatial convergence are established theoretically and verified numerically.
conclusion: The proposed method is stable and achieves high-order accuracy for variable-order time-fractional subdiffusion interface problems.

title: The Purpose Of Mathematics According To Plato And Augustine
authors: Douglas J. Dailey
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1973, Russian mathematician I.R. Shafarevitch delivered a lecture to the G\"ottingen Academy of Sciences on the purpose of mathematics. The conclusion he reached in his address is that the ultimate purpose of mathematics must be religious. In this talk, we will explore a possible way in which this claim can be justified by understanding the purpose that mathematics served within a person's intellectual formation according to Plato. To place Plato's view into a Christian perspective, we will then investigate the thought of St. Augustine of Hippo, the great fifth century theologian and bishop. Augustine's insight on the role that number plays in the development of reason sheds light on how knowledge of mathematics conduces to knowledge of God.
tldr: This paper discusses the philosophical and religious purpose of mathematics according to Plato and Augustine, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The author aims to justify Shafarevitch's claim that the ultimate purpose of mathematics is religious, by exploring Plato's and Augustine's views on mathematics and its role in intellectual and spiritual formation.
method: The paper presents a philosophical analysis and comparison of Plato's and Augustine's writings on mathematics, number, and their relation to the divine.
result: The paper argues that mathematics serves a religious purpose by conducing to knowledge of God, as seen in the works of Plato and Augustine.
conclusion: Mathematics has a religious purpose, and understanding its role in intellectual formation can lead to knowledge of God.

title: Comparing Scalar Objective Functions For Multi-Criteria Engineering Optimization
authors: Olaf Frommann
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalar objective functions are required when a multi-criteria optimization problem must yield a single preferred design rather than only a Pareto set. The choice of scalarization influences which compromise is selected, how preference parameters are interpreted, and whether non-supported Pareto regions can be reached. This paper compares four formulations for normalized bi-criteria minimization: weighted sums, achievement scalarizing functions, desirability functions, and a fuzzy-logic-based formulation. Two analytically defined Pareto fronts, one convex and one concave, isolate the effect of the objective formulation from numerical optimizer behavior. The comparison focuses on reachable Pareto regions, parameter-induced selection density, compensation between criteria, sensitivity, and interpretability. Results show that weighted sums are simple but structurally limited on concave fronts, while achievement, desirability, and fuzzy formulations reach interior non-supported regions through different mechanisms. Desirability functions introduce nonlinear single-criterion preference mappings, whereas fuzzy rules express nonseparable and reference-dependent engineering preferences.
tldr: This paper compares scalar objective functions for multi-criteria engineering optimization, focusing on Pareto front reachability and parameter sensitivity.
motivation: Multi-criteria optimization often requires a single preferred design, and the choice of scalarization method affects which compromise is selected.
method: Four scalarization formulations (weighted sums, achievement scalarizing functions, desirability functions, fuzzy-logic) are compared on two analytically defined Pareto fronts (convex and concave).
result: Weighted sums are structurally limited on concave fronts, while other formulations reach non-supported regions through different mechanisms.
conclusion: The choice of scalarization significantly impacts the selected compromise and interpretability, with desirability and fuzzy methods offering more flexibility.

title: A New Noise Model For Data-driven Control: Generalized Frobenius Norm Bounds
authors: Huayuan Huang, M. Kanat Camlibel, Henk J. van Waarde
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we introduce a new noise model for data-driven control. The model can be interpreted as a generalization of a Frobenius norm bound on the matrix of noise samples. For instantaneously bounded noise, the proposed model provides a less conservative overapproximation than an existing noise model based on a quadratic matrix inequality (QMI). Using the new model, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for data-driven control. The framework covers a broad class of design problems, including quadratic stabilization, [MATH] control and [MATH] control, and is further extended to cover data-driven analysis problems, ranging for stabilizability to dissipativity. A key technical contribution is a new type of S-lemma that offers necessary and sufficient conditions under which a quadratic matrix inequality is implied by a quadratic inequality in vectorized variables.
tldr: This paper introduces a new noise model for data-driven control based on generalized Frobenius norm bounds, with applications to quadratic stabilization and H-infinity control.
motivation: Existing noise models for data-driven control may be overly conservative; a more flexible model is needed to improve controller design under instantaneously bounded noise.
method: The authors propose a noise model that generalizes Frobenius norm bounds on the noise matrix, and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for data-driven control using a new S-lemma for quadratic matrix inequalities.
result: The new model provides less conservative overapproximations than QMI-based models, and the framework covers quadratic stabilization, H2 and H-infinity control, as well as analysis problems like stabilizability and dissipativity.
conclusion: The proposed noise model and S-lemma offer a unified and less conservative approach to data-driven control, with potential for broader application in control theory.

title: A Relaxation And Rectification (ReCR) Framework For Systems With Linear And Complementary Constraints: Theoretical Foundation, Algorithms And Numerical Experiments
authors: Wissam Alali, Xin Jiang, Jiming Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Systems defined by linear and complementarity constraints (SLCCs) arise frequently in engineering, economics, and other related fields. They also appear in the optimality conditions of many challenging optimization models, such as bilinear optimization and linearly constrained quadratic optimization. It is known that finding a feasible solution to an SLCC is NP-hard in general. In this paper, we study the feasibility problem for a given SLCC: either find a feasible solution or determine that the system is infeasible. To this end, we introduce a universal relaxation theory (URT), which reformulates SLCC feasibility as an equivalent bilinear optimization problem with linear constraints in a lifted space. We then analyze the resulting bilinear model and derive necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for its global solutions. Based on these theoretical insights, we introduce a relaxation-rectification (ReCR) framework for finding a feasible solution to a given SLCC instance or certifying infeasibility. We develop several ReCR methods that differ in their working spaces and subproblem formulations and analyze their convergence properties. We also develop a numerical procedure for obtaining an infeasibility certificate when the ReCR methods do not find a feasible solution. We conduct numerical experiments to evaluate the reliability, robustness, and scalability of the proposed ReCR methods and compare them with existing SLCC solvers. On the tested small- and large-scale LCP instances from the literature, the proposed ReCR methods typically find feasible solutions in a few iterations. We also extend the benchmark with more challenging medium-scale SLCC instances, on which the proposed hybrid ReCR (H-ReCR) method exhibits promising performance.
tldr: This paper proposes a relaxation-rectification framework for solving systems with linear and complementarity constraints, which is an optimization problem unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Systems with linear and complementarity constraints (SLCCs) arise in engineering and economics, and finding feasible solutions is NP-hard. The authors aim to develop a universal relaxation theory and efficient algorithms.
method: The paper introduces a universal relaxation theory that reformulates SLCC feasibility as a bilinear optimization problem with linear constraints in a lifted space, then develops relaxation-rectification (ReCR) methods with convergence analysis.
result: Numerical experiments show that the proposed ReCR methods find feasible solutions in few iterations for small- and large-scale LCP instances, and the hybrid ReCR method performs well on challenging medium-scale instances.
conclusion: The ReCR framework provides a reliable and scalable approach for solving SLCCs, with potential applications in optimization and related fields.

title: A Sharp Kato-Rosenblum Type Theorem For Unbounded n-Tuples
authors: Dan Virgil Voiculescu Rhishab Bhutani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a generalization for commuting [MATH]-tuples of unbounded self-adjoint operators and the Lorentz [MATH] ideal,[MATH], of the Kato-Rosenblum theorem. The result is derived from earlier work for bounded operators [8]. Also, a very weak result for [MATH] unbounded operators and other additional results are obtained.
tldr: This paper proves a generalization of the Kato-Rosenblum theorem for unbounded operator tuples, a result in operator theory.
motivation: The Kato-Rosenblum theorem is a classical result in perturbation theory; the authors aim to extend it to unbounded n-tuples of commuting self-adjoint operators.
method: The proof builds on earlier work for bounded operators and uses techniques from operator theory and functional analysis.
result: A sharp Kato-Rosenblum type theorem is established for unbounded n-tuples, along with some weaker results for general unbounded operators.
conclusion: The work contributes to the mathematical theory of operators but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: An Adaptive Fast Algorithm For Periodic Coulomb Lattice Sums In Arbitrary Unit Cells
authors: Xuanzhao Gao, Leslie Greengard, Shidong Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a fast algorithm for evaluating conditionally convergent Coulomb lattice sums, governed by the Laplace equation with periodic boundary conditions on arbitrary unit cells (oblique in 2D, triclinic in 3D) and arbitrary particle distributions. The algorithm extends the dual-space multilevel kernel-splitting (DMK) framework to this context. The root of the adaptive tree is now a rectangular grid of cubes consisting of an inner block covering the unit cell and a surrounding halo of image cubes, rather than a single cube, and the smooth top-level periodic kernel -- the only term that requires the consideration of conditional convergence issues -- is evaluated by the ``five-step procedure" used in fast Ewald summation: spreading, fast Fourier transform (FFT), diagonal scaling, inverse FFT, and interpolation. The resulting complexity is [MATH] for fixed cell shape. Benchmarked against the periodic fast multipole method on highly nonuniform source distributions, our 2D algorithm is roughly an order of magnitude faster across particle counts and target precisions; in three dimensions, it is often as fast as the free-space DMK on the same sources, even for triclinic cells with edge-length ratios up to roughly [MATH].
tldr: A fast algorithm for evaluating periodic Coulomb lattice sums in arbitrary unit cells.
motivation: Efficient computation of electrostatic interactions in periodic systems is needed for molecular dynamics and materials science.
method: Extends the dual-space multilevel kernel-splitting (DMK) framework with an adaptive tree and five-step Ewald summation procedure.
result: The algorithm achieves O(N log N) complexity and is an order of magnitude faster than the periodic fast multipole method for nonuniform distributions.
conclusion: The method provides a fast and accurate solution for periodic Coulomb sums in arbitrary unit cells.

title: Derivative Of The Jacobi Polynomials With Respect To Their Order And Applications To Indefinite Integration
authors: Axel Schulze-Halberg
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We calculate the first derivative of the Jacobi polynomials with respect to their order in explicit form. This derivative is not an elementary function, but contains elementary special cases. As an application, we use our result with a recently devised method for resolving a new class of indefinite integrals containing Jacobi polynomials.
tldr: This paper computes the derivative of Jacobi polynomials with respect to their order and applies it to indefinite integration.
motivation: To obtain an explicit expression for the derivative of Jacobi polynomials with respect to order, which is not elementary, and to use it for solving a new class of integrals.
method: Analytical derivation using known properties of Jacobi polynomials and special functions.
result: An explicit formula for the first derivative of Jacobi polynomials with respect to order, with elementary special cases, and its application to indefinite integrals.
conclusion: The derivative formula enables the resolution of certain indefinite integrals containing Jacobi polynomials.

title: Paper Fortune Tellers In Julia Sets Of Generalized McMullen Maps Ii: Sidecars And Zippers
authors: Kelsey Brouwer Suzanne Boyd
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the family of complex rational functions known as Generalized McMullen maps, F(z) = z^n + a/z^n+b, for integer n at least 3 fixed, and complex parameters a, b with a nonzero. In prior work by the same authors, we provided a combinatorial model for a large class of maps whose Julia sets contain both infinitely many homeomorphic copies of quadratic Julia sets conjugate to the ``basilica'', and infinitely many subsets homeomorphic to a set which is obtained by starting with the basilica, then changing a finite number of pairs of external ray landing point identifications, following an algorithm we described. In this article, we generalize beyond the basilica, and provide a catalog of additional types of hyperbolic Julia sets of Generalized McMullen maps, where the ``baby'' Julia set can be any rabbit, aeroplane, or Kokopelli quadratic Julia set; that is, where the c-value can be taken from any bulb attached to the main cardioid of the Mandelbrot set, or from the main cardioid of any principal baby Mandelbrot set (no renormalizations).
tldr: This paper studies combinatorial models of Julia sets for generalized McMullen maps, focusing on baby Julia sets that are quadratic-like.
motivation: To extend prior work on basilica-type Julia sets to a broader class of hyperbolic Julia sets in the family of generalized McMullen maps.
method: The authors provide a catalog of baby Julia sets corresponding to various quadratic Julia sets (rabbit, aeroplane, Kokopelli) by analyzing parameter space and external ray identifications.
result: They show that infinitely many homeomorphic copies of these quadratic Julia sets appear in the Julia sets of generalized McMullen maps.
conclusion: The work generalizes the combinatorial model to include a wider variety of baby Julia sets, but remains within complex dynamics and does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Revisiting Local Regression: Shape Regularity, Uniform Rates, And The Limits Of Random Splits
authors: J\'er\'emy Bettinger, Fran\c{c}ois Portier, Adrien Saumard
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Considering pointwise and sup-norm estimation, we analyze the non-asymptotic behavior of local averaging estimators for Lipschitz regression functions. Building on a general deviation bound for estimators based on a VC family of localizing sets, we introduce the notion of shape-regular local maps, where averaging is performed over sets with an almost isotropic geometry. Our main message is a characterization: shape regularity is both necessary and sufficient to attain optimal rates, up to logarithmic factors. Necessity is established non-asymptotically through an explicit anisotropic example, sharpening a phenomenon previously understood only heuristically in asymptotic theory. We then draw two consequences. First, the simple [MATH]-nearest neighbor rule is shape-regular by construction and attains the optimal rate, even on unbounded supports. Second, and perhaps surprisingly, the popular random-split condition for trees -- known to ensure consistency and vanishing cell diameters -- does not guarantee optimal rates: for blind tree constructions, the cell aspect ratio diverges exponentially with depth, so that shape regularity fails with positive probability. This identifies the absence of a geometric correction mechanism, rather than a slowly shrinking diameter, as the obstruction to optimality. Motivated by this gap, we propose a tree construction that enforces shape regularity through a simple constraint on admissible splits, and prove a uniform deviation inequality showing that it restores the optimal rate for Lipschitz functions.
tldr: This paper studies non-asymptotic rates for local regression estimators, focusing on shape regularity and random splits in trees.
motivation: To understand when local averaging estimators achieve optimal rates for Lipschitz regression, and to identify why random-split trees fail to do so.
method: Derives a general deviation bound for VC-class localizing sets, introduces shape-regular local maps, and analyzes nearest-neighbor and tree-based estimators.
result: Shape regularity is necessary and sufficient for optimal rates; random-split trees fail due to diverging aspect ratios, not slow diameter shrinkage.
conclusion: A tree construction enforcing shape regularity restores optimal rates, highlighting the importance of geometric correction.

title: Composition Semigroups On Bmoa And $H^{\infty}$
authors: Austin Anderson, Mirjana Jovovic, Wayne Smith
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study [MATH], the maximal space of strong continuity for a semigroup of composition operators induced by a semigroup [MATH] of analytic self-maps of the unit disk, when [MATH] is BMOA, [MATH] or the disk algebra. In particular, we show that [MATH] for all nontrivial semigroups. We also prove, for every semigroup [MATH], that [MATH] not just pointwise, but in [MATH] norm. This provides a unified proof of known results about [MATH] when [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies composition semigroups on function spaces BMOA and H∞, which is a topic in complex analysis and operator theory.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize the maximal space of strong continuity for semigroups of composition operators on certain analytic function spaces.
method: They analyze semigroups of analytic self-maps of the unit disk and their induced composition operators, proving convergence in norm on BMOA and the disk algebra.
result: They show that for all nontrivial semigroups, the maximal space of strong continuity is BMOA, and that convergence holds in norm.
conclusion: The work provides a unified proof of known results and extends them to BMOA and the disk algebra.

title: A Trace-Based Interface Reduction Method For Highly Conducting Interfaces
authors: Do Young Kwak So-Hsiang Chou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a reduced interface formulation for elliptic interface problems with highly conducting interfaces. The interface condition consists of continuity of the primal variable together with a jump in the normal flux proportional to the surface Laplacian of the interface trace. Instead of using the solution jump as the interface unknown, we employ the common interface trace and derive a trace-based Schur complement formulation. For prescribed interface trace data, independent extension problems are solved in the two subdomains, leading to a reduced interface equation involving the Dirichlet-to-Neumann jump operator and a surface stiffness operator. Finite-dimensional trace approximations produce compact reduced systems posed only on the interface. Numerical experiments for circular, smooth noncircular, and heart-shaped interfaces illustrate the effectiveness of the method and the role of interface-mode enrichment.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for elliptic interface problems with highly conducting interfaces, focusing on computational efficiency.
motivation: Efficiently solving elliptic interface problems with highly conducting interfaces is important in many engineering applications, but existing methods can be computationally expensive.
method: The authors develop a trace-based Schur complement formulation that reduces the interface problem to a compact system involving the Dirichlet-to-Neumann jump operator and a surface stiffness operator.
result: Numerical experiments on circular, smooth noncircular, and heart-shaped interfaces demonstrate the effectiveness of the method and the role of interface-mode enrichment.
conclusion: The proposed trace-based interface reduction method provides an efficient and accurate approach for solving elliptic interface problems with highly conducting interfaces.

title: Brownian Bridge Diffusion-Based Joint Channel Estimation And Data Detection For Jamming-Resilient Receivers
authors: Honghan She, Yufan Cheng, Tieming Sun, Pengyu Wang, Siya Huang, Kaikai Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In next-generation wireless networks, the growing density of devices and limited spectrum resources pose severe jamming challenges to fragile legitimate communication links in the wireless electromagnetic environment. Crucially, when jamming overlaps with pilot and data symbols in both time and frequency domains, it inflicts a severe bottleneck on receiver-side joint estimation and detection. Existing schemes often lack an effective framework to combat such jamming contamination, thereby failing to guarantee reliable transmission. To address this issue, we propose a Brownian bridge diffusion-based joint channel estimation and data detection framework (BBD-JCED) for jamming-resilient receivers. Specifically, the proposed framework comprises two core modules: the first extracts jamming features in the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) domain and suppresses jamming samples, thereby improving the signal-to-jamming-plus-noise ratio (SJNR) of the received signal; the second introduces a Brownian bridge diffusion (BBD) process to model the evolution of the suppressed signal and the encoded bits in the presence of channel estimation errors, thereby enabling enhanced joint channel estimation and data detection. To alleviate the computational burden of the BBD process in the second module, we further derive a fast ordinary differential equation (ODE) solver that enables its low-complexity iterative evolution. Finally, we design a multi-module training algorithm to improve the data recovery capability of the proposed framework. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior bit recovery performance compared with baseline schemes while maintaining a lower number of model parameters and competitive computational complexity.
tldr: This paper proposes a Brownian bridge diffusion-based framework for joint channel estimation and data detection in jamming-resilient wireless receivers.
motivation: Next-generation wireless networks face severe jamming challenges that degrade joint estimation and detection, especially when jamming overlaps with pilot and data symbols.
method: The framework extracts jamming features in the STFT domain and suppresses them, then uses a Brownian bridge diffusion process to model signal evolution with channel estimation errors, with a fast ODE solver for low-complexity iteration.
result: Simulations show superior bit recovery performance compared to baselines, with fewer model parameters and competitive computational complexity.
conclusion: The proposed BBD-JCED framework effectively enhances jamming resilience and reliable transmission in wireless networks.

title: Viscosity In Error Upper Bound For A Consistent Splitting Scheme Of The Navier-Stokes Equations
authors: M Nader Alhomsi, Jiahong Wu, Xiaoming Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the role of viscosity in the error upper bounds of a consistent splitting scheme for the Navier-Stokes equations proposed by Huang and Shen [5]. In their original analysis the viscosity is fixed to unity. By following and extending their proof methodology while keeping the viscosity symbolic, we obtain an H1 velocity error bound that contains negative powers of viscosity, indicating that the scheme is not robust as viscosity tends zero. To establish this bound we refine a theorem in [8] on the constant in the Stokes pressure estimate, which is crucial to the error analysis. A targeted numerical experiment based on a perturbation of the Kovasznay flow corroborates this analytical prediction: the scheme of [5] blows up at high Reynolds number, and a comparison with a fully implicit Newton solver and with the time-dependent Stokes counterpart of the same scheme localizes the failure to the explicit treatment of the convection term.
tldr: This paper analyzes the viscosity dependence of error bounds for a splitting scheme of the Navier-Stokes equations, showing blow-up at high Reynolds number.
motivation: The original analysis fixed viscosity to unity; this work extends it to understand robustness as viscosity tends to zero.
method: The authors refine a theorem on the constant in the Stokes pressure estimate and perform numerical experiments on a perturbed Kovasznay flow.
result: The H1 velocity error bound contains negative powers of viscosity, indicating non-robustness; numerical tests confirm blow-up at high Reynolds number.
conclusion: The splitting scheme fails for high Reynolds numbers due to explicit treatment of the convection term, and a fully implicit Newton solver is more robust.

title: On Strong Algebrability And Spaceability Of Continuous Functions And Fractal Dimensions
authors: Saisai Shi Jia Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the strong algebrability and [MATH]-lineability/spaceability of continuous functions with prescribed fractal dimensions. For [MATH], we define $[MATH][MATH][MATH][MATH][MATH][MATH]H_s[0,1]\cap_r[0,1]\cap_t[0,1][MATH][MATH]1<s\leq t\leq2[MATH]H_s[0,1]\cap_t[0,1][MATH](p,)[MATH]p=1,2[MATH]H_s[0,1]\cap_t[0,1][MATH](n,m+n)[MATH]m,n\in$, thus complementing the recent work of Liu et al. .
tldr: This paper studies strong algebrability and spaceability of continuous functions with prescribed fractal dimensions, which is a topic in functional analysis and fractal geometry.
motivation: The authors aim to investigate the algebraic and linear structures within sets of continuous functions that have specific fractal dimensions, complementing recent work by Liu et al.
method: They define function spaces H_s[0,1] and related intersections, and prove results on strong algebrability and lineability/spaceability using constructions of functions with prescribed fractal dimensions.
result: They show that certain sets of continuous functions with given fractal dimensions are strongly algebrable and spaceable, providing explicit examples.
conclusion: The work contributes to the understanding of the algebraic structure of function spaces with fractal constraints, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Estimating The Tail Of The Singular Product For The Hardy Littlewood And Bateman Horn Conjectures
authors: Victor Volfson
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior of the tail of the singular product arising in the Hardy Littlewood and Bateman Horn conjectures for one dimensional systems of polynomials. A universal estimate is proved, showing that the contribution of large primes decays like the reciprocal of the logarithm, regardless of the structure of the system. For linear systems (trivial Galois group) superfast convergence is obtained. For nonlinear systems a coefficient is defined that is expressed via the average over the Galois group; in the abelian case and under the Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L functions a more precise error estimate is obtained. Mixed systems containing both linear and nonlinear polynomials are also considered. Numerical experiments, presented as summary tables, confirm the theoretical conclusions. The results provide a rigorous theoretical foundation for computing singular series and refine the Bateman Horn formula.
tldr: This paper studies the tail behavior of singular products in number theory conjectures, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To provide rigorous estimates for the singular series in Hardy-Littlewood and Bateman-Horn conjectures, which are important in analytic number theory.
method: The author proves universal estimates for the tail of the singular product using analytic number theory techniques, including Galois group averages and conditional results under the Riemann Hypothesis.
result: The contribution of large primes decays like 1/log n, with faster convergence for linear systems and refined estimates for abelian nonlinear systems under the Riemann Hypothesis.
conclusion: The results provide a theoretical foundation for computing singular series and refine the Bateman-Horn formula, but are unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fast Unified Evaluation Of Layer And Volume Potentials For The 2d Modified Helmholtz Equation
authors: Edith Frisk G\"artner, Fredrik Fryklund, Anna-Karin Tornberg
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a fast and accurate potential theory-based method for the two-dimensional modified Helmholtz equation, treating the involved singular and nearly singular layer evaluations together with volume potentials within a single computational framework. The method is based on a decomposition of the free-space Green's function into a short-range local part and a smooth long-range part. The long-range contribution is evaluated efficiently using the non-uniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT), while the local contribution is treated by asymptotic expansions. For the layer potentials, an intermediate telescoping sum over dyadic refinement levels is added, where the resulting difference kernels are smooth and rapidly decaying, allowing the dyadic levels to be evaluated without specialized quadrature rules. The volume potential is evaluated on triangular cut-cell meshes, where the mesh only enters the scheme as quadrature rule for smooth data. This makes the method robust with respect to small and distorted mesh cells, without the need for stabilization or cell-merging techniques. Numerical experiments demonstrate the expected convergence rates, high throughput of the potential evaluations, and robustness with respect to mesh quality.
tldr: This paper presents a fast numerical method for evaluating layer and volume potentials for the 2D modified Helmholtz equation.
motivation: Efficient and accurate evaluation of potentials is crucial for boundary integral methods and volume potential solvers, but existing methods often struggle with singularities and mesh quality.
method: The method decomposes the Green's function into short-range local and smooth long-range parts, using NUFFT for long-range and asymptotic expansions for local contributions, with a telescoping sum for layer potentials.
result: Numerical experiments show expected convergence rates, high throughput, and robustness to mesh quality without stabilization.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a fast, accurate, and robust unified approach for potential evaluations in 2D modified Helmholtz problems.

title: Devil's Terraces: Determining The Organization Of Resonance Tongues In A Periodically Forced Dynamical System
authors: John Bailie, Priya Subramanian, Bernd Krauskopf
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In periodically forced dynamical systems, resonance tongues are open regions of a parameter plane in which the dynamics on an invariant torus locks to a stable periodic orbit. While individual resonance tongues are well understood, the principles governing their global arrangement remain largely unexplored. We develop a topological framework, grounded in applied topology and Morse theory, whose central object is the two-dimensional resonance surface, defined as the graph of the rotation number [MATH] over a parameter plane. Within this framework, resonance tongues appear as terraces of the resonance surface at rational values of [MATH], and their global arrangement is determined by the singularities of this surface. Resolving the resonance surface requires the accurate computation of [MATH], and we present an algorithm that does so efficiently and at high resolution. As a specific example, we examine a periodically forced model of vertical mixing in the North Atlantic, a process relevant to the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, and study how its resonance surface changes under variation of a third parameter. We identify six distinct resonance-tongue arrangements and show that the resonance transitions between them are due to changes in the number and type of singularities on the boundary of the resonance surface.
tldr: This paper studies resonance tongues in periodically forced dynamical systems using topological methods, with an application to ocean mixing.
motivation: The global arrangement of resonance tongues in parameter planes is not well understood, and the authors aim to develop a topological framework to explain their organization.
method: They define a resonance surface as the graph of the rotation number over a parameter plane, compute it efficiently with a high-resolution algorithm, and analyze its singularities using Morse theory.
result: Six distinct resonance-tongue arrangements are identified, and transitions between them are linked to changes in the number and type of singularities on the boundary of the resonance surface.
conclusion: The topological framework successfully explains the global organization of resonance tongues and can be applied to other periodically forced systems.

title: Splitting Schemes For Problems With Memory
authors: Petr N. Vabishchevich
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper considers the Cauchy problem for a first-order integro-differential equation with memory in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space. The main computational difficulty of such problems is the need to store and process the solution at all previous time levels. To overcome this difficulty, an approach is used that approximates the memory kernel by a sum of exponentials, which reduces the original nonlocal problem to a local one -- a system of weakly coupled evolution equations with additional ordinary differential equations for auxiliary functions. The problem is formulated in vector form on the direct sum of Hilbert spaces. Unconditional stability of two-level operator-difference schemes with weights is proved under standard restrictions. Splitting schemes are proposed and investigated by separating the local and integral operators of the problem. Possibilities for constructing similar schemes for other nonlocal problems, in particular for the equation with memory of the time derivative of the solution, are noted.
tldr: The paper proposes splitting schemes for solving integro-differential equations with memory by approximating the memory kernel with exponentials.
motivation: Computational difficulty arises from storing and processing the solution at all previous time levels for problems with memory.
method: The memory kernel is approximated by a sum of exponentials, reducing the nonlocal problem to a local system of weakly coupled evolution equations. Two-level operator-difference schemes with weights are analyzed, and splitting schemes are proposed by separating local and integral operators.
result: Unconditional stability of the schemes is proved under standard restrictions.
conclusion: The approach can be extended to other nonlocal problems, such as equations with memory of the time derivative.

title: Second-Order Sensitivity Of Efficient Solution And Marginal Maps In Parametric Vector Optimization With Set Constraints
authors: Tan H. Cao N. X. D. Bao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a second-order sensitivity theory for the efficient solution map \(S\) of a parametric vector optimization problem \(\min_C f(p,x)\) subject to \(x\in H(p)\). The main point is the passage from efficient values to efficient decisions. Under a value-to-decision error bound (VDB), second-order information for the marginal map \(\Phi\) lifts to a second-order Dini formula for \(S\). We first work in the abstract inclusion model \(x\in H(p)\), where outer and inner estimates yield second-order semi-derivability of \(S\). We then specialize to structured feasible maps \(H(p)=\{x\in\Omega:g(p,x)\in D\}\). Under Robinson metric regularity along \(\Omega\), second-order regularity of \(\Omega\) and \(D\), and directional second-order semi-derivability of the data, we obtain explicit formulas for \(\DD H\), \(\DD\Phi\), and \(\DD S\). The framework is specialized to polyhedral inequality/equality systems and illustrated by a robust multi-objective portfolio model and a DC-dispatch model for electricity markets, with a brief discussion of complementarity-based extensions.
tldr: This paper develops second-order sensitivity theory for efficient solutions and marginal maps in parametric vector optimization with set constraints.
motivation: To extend sensitivity analysis from scalar to vector optimization, enabling second-order approximations of efficient decision maps under perturbations.
method: Uses a value-to-decision error bound (VDB) to lift second-order information from marginal maps to efficient solution maps, and applies Robinson metric regularity for structured constraints.
result: Derives second-order Dini formulas for the efficient solution map and marginal map under polyhedral and DC-dispatch models.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical framework for second-order sensitivity in multi-objective optimization, with applications to portfolio and electricity market models.

title: Faster Than Fast-LTS: Robust Regression And Outlier Detection With Dc Programming
authors: Marah-Lisanne Thormann, Phan Tu Vuong, Alain B. Zemkoho, Tri-Dung Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When datasets contain outliers, robust regression is a well-established alternative to Ordinary Least Squares. A commonly employed robust estimator is Least Trimmed Squares (LTS), which computes the regression coefficients from a subset of observations. Determining the exact solution corresponds to a combinatorial problem with prohibitive computational costs, even for instances of moderate dimension. Thus, the most prevalent approach in practice remains a heuristic known as Fast-LTS. Although the heuristic often performs effectively, certain elements of the approach remain open to improvement. In particular, its core procedure provides robust results only when initialized with a large number of starting points. To address the heuristic's limitations, this paper reformulates the LTS problem as a concave minimization problem subject to a capped simplex constraint, and proposes the successive Boosted Difference of Convex Functions Algorithm (sBDCA) as a solution method. Theoretically, we establish via the \L ojasiewicz property that sBDCA converges to a local solution with a linear rate in the fastest case. To ensure robustness from a single initialization in practice, we derive and integrate a problem-specific preconditioning matrix into the algorithmic setup. Building on this theoretical foundation, we conduct numerical studies on various synthetic and real-world datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of sBDCA with preconditioning. Specifically, we show that our approach is up to 3.25 times faster than Fast-LTS and achieves up to 90% lower objective function values, particularly in high-dimensional settings. As all code is openly available, this paper further provides a practical guide to robust regression in Python.
tldr: This paper proposes a new algorithm for robust regression and outlier detection using difference of convex functions programming, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper addresses the computational limitations of the Fast-LTS heuristic for robust regression, aiming to improve speed and solution quality.
method: The authors reformulate the Least Trimmed Squares problem as a concave minimization with a capped simplex constraint and develop the successive Boosted Difference of Convex Functions Algorithm (sBDCA) with preconditioning.
result: The proposed method is up to 3.25 times faster than Fast-LTS and achieves up to 90% lower objective function values, especially in high-dimensional settings.
conclusion: The sBDCA algorithm with preconditioning offers a more efficient and robust alternative to Fast-LTS for robust regression.

title: A Mass, Momentum, And Energy Conserving Semi-Lagrangian Adaptive-Rank (slar) Method For The Vlasov-Poisson System
authors: Nanyi Zheng, William A. Sands, Jing-Mei Qiu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a semi-Lagrangian adaptive-rank (SLAR) method that combines the large time-step capability of semi-Lagrangian schemes with the efficiency of adaptive-rank tensor representations while simultaneously enforcing local conservation laws for mass, momentum, and energy. The method builds on the high-dimensional SLAR framework introduced in our previous work and achieves high-order accuracy in both space and time. To address the loss of conservation in long-time simulations, we extend the implicit local macroscopic conservative (LoMaC) correction technique for the BGK equation to the high-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson (VP) system. The implicit macroscopic system is discretized using backward differentiation formulas and solved with a Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov method. This approach enables a consistent coupling with semi-Lagrangian methods which are capable of taking large time steps. A novel component of the proposed method is a unified adaptive-weight projection technique that eliminates the ad hoc parameter tuning required by previous LoMaC approaches. These weights capture problem-dependent velocity space structures and are constructed from the low-rank velocity bases of the solution. The local semi-Lagrangian method used in this work reconstructs the solution at the feet of the characteristics using efficient tensor contractions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first successful implementation of an implicit LoMaC method for the VP system up to the 2D--2V setting. Numerical experiments on several classical benchmark problems demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method, as well as its ability to preserve conservation laws in VP simulations.
tldr: This paper presents a semi-Lagrangian adaptive-rank method for the Vlasov-Poisson system that enforces mass, momentum, and energy conservation.
motivation: The Vlasov-Poisson system is a fundamental model in plasma physics, and numerical methods that preserve conservation laws are crucial for accurate long-time simulations.
method: The method combines semi-Lagrangian schemes with adaptive-rank tensor representations and extends the implicit local macroscopic conservative (LoMaC) correction technique to the VP system, using a unified adaptive-weight projection and a Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov solver.
result: Numerical experiments on benchmark problems demonstrate accuracy, efficiency, and conservation of mass, momentum, and energy in 2D-2V settings.
conclusion: The proposed SLAR method is the first successful implementation of an implicit LoMaC method for the VP system, offering a promising approach for kinetic plasma simulations.

title: An Approximate Conjugate Subgradient Algorithm With Matrix Parameter For Derivative-Free Nonsmooth Optimization Problems
authors: Morteza Kimiaei, Saman Babaie-Kafaki, Zohre Aminifard
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a derivative-free matrix conjugate-subgradient method for unconstrained nonsmooth optimization of locally Lipschitz functions. The method constructs discrete gradients using only function values and forms a finite sampled model of the Goldstein subdifferential. A minimal-norm element of the convex hull of the sampled discrete gradients is then computed and used both as a stationarity measure and as the reference vector for generating descent-oriented directions. To improve robustness beyond the basic steepest-descent direction, we introduce a matrix memory correction together with coefficient damping, diagonal scaling, bounded-angle correction, and matrix-stability safeguards. A two-point line-search procedure with enrichment is used to obtain either a serious step or an improved local model. Under suitable consistency assumptions on the discrete-gradient approximation and line-search sampling, the method generates directions satisfying a safeguarded descent property and computes approximate Goldstein stationary points. Numerical experiments on nonsmooth test problems with dimensions up to 1000 show that both proposed variants are robust for lower and medium accuracy requirements, while the matrix conjugate-subgradient variant remains the most reliable under the strictest tolerance.
tldr: This paper proposes a derivative-free conjugate subgradient method for nonsmooth optimization, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to solve unconstrained nonsmooth optimization problems for locally Lipschitz functions without requiring derivative information.
method: It constructs discrete gradients using function values, forms a sampled model of the Goldstein subdifferential, and uses a matrix memory correction with safeguards to generate descent directions.
result: Numerical experiments on test problems up to dimension 1000 show robustness for lower and medium accuracy requirements.
conclusion: The matrix conjugate-subgradient variant is reliable under strict tolerances, but the work is purely in classical optimization.

title: Plaa: Packet-level Adversarial Attacks In Network Traffic Detection
authors: Jinhao You, Zan Zhou, Shujie Yang, Yi Sun, Lei Zhang, Changqiao Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are widely applied in Network-based Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) due to their high accuracy. However, DNNs are highly susceptible to adversarial attacks, which generate malicious traffic to evade NIDS detection. Existing approaches often adapt adversarial attacks from computer vision (CV) tasks to the NIDS domain, overlooking the fundamental differences between CV and NIDS. This results in two major issues: 1) The generated network traffic may become invalid, 2) The generated traffic may lose its original attack semantics. To address these issues, this paper proposes an adversarial attack specifically designed for NIDS. Instead of directly generating flow-level features, our approach incrementally generates packet-level features to construct adversarial traffic. During the generation process, the semantic integrity of the traffic is monitored at each stage, effectively avoiding the issues of invalid traffic and semantic loss observed in existing methods. We evaluate our attack algorithm against current NIDS models using the CIC-UNSW-NB15, CIC-DDoS2019, and CIC-IDS-2017 datasets. The proposed method achieves an average evasion success rate of 92.78%, while ensuring that the generated adversarial traffic remains semantically consistent with the original malicious traffic.
tldr: This paper proposes a packet-level adversarial attack method for network intrusion detection systems, focusing on generating semantically valid adversarial traffic.
motivation: Existing adversarial attacks adapted from computer vision often produce invalid network traffic or lose attack semantics, limiting their effectiveness against NIDS.
method: The approach incrementally generates packet-level features while monitoring semantic integrity at each stage to ensure the generated traffic remains valid and retains original attack semantics.
result: The proposed method achieves an average evasion success rate of 92.78% on three benchmark datasets while maintaining semantic consistency with original malicious traffic.
conclusion: The packet-level generation with semantic monitoring effectively addresses the issues of invalid traffic and semantic loss, providing a more realistic adversarial attack for NIDS evaluation.

title: KoAT: Automatic Complexity And Termination Analysis Of Integer Programs
authors: Nils Lommen, \'el\'eanore Meyer, J\"urgen Giesl
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: KoAT is a tool to automatically infer complexity bounds and prove termination of (possibly recursive) integer programs. To this end, KoAT implements an alternating modular inference of upper runtime and size bounds for program parts. In particular, KoAT uses a portfolio of different techniques to analyze subprograms. The power of our approach is demonstrated by an extensive experimental evaluation.
tldr: KoAT is a tool for automatic complexity and termination analysis of integer programs, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to automate the inference of runtime and size bounds for integer programs, which is a problem in program analysis and verification.
method: KoAT uses an alternating modular inference of upper runtime and size bounds, employing a portfolio of techniques to analyze subprograms.
result: The tool demonstrates effectiveness through extensive experimental evaluation on integer programs.
conclusion: KoAT provides a practical solution for automatic complexity and termination analysis, but it is not relevant to the user's research interests.

title: In-Vehicle Digital Twin-Based Collision Warning Framework With Sybil Attack Detection
authors: Mohammad Imtiaz Hasan, Abyad Enan, Jean Michel Tine, Araf Rahman, M Sabbir Salek, Mashrur Chowdhury
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Connected Vehicles (CVs) rely extensively on communication technologies to enable data-driven predictive analyses for enhancing performance and safety. These communication channels can be exploited by adversaries to launch cyberattacks such as Sybil attacks, which could threaten both safety-critical and mobility applications, leaving CVs vulnerable and putting human lives at risk.
