As CV deployment continues to expand, the need to detect and mitigate cyberattacks in real-time becomes increasingly urgent. This study presents an in-vehicle Digital Twin (DT)-based collision warning framework with built-in capabilities for Sybil attacks detection. The framework integrates a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) for learning temporal dependencies in vehicle trajectory data and Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) algorithms for efficient similarity-based classification. Our framework is evaluated on real-world Sybil attack data, collected through field experiments. The framework achieved accuracy, recall, and F1 scores of 0.984, 1.00, and 0.944, respectively, in detecting Sybil-generated fake vehicles. During the safety evaluation, the framework reduced the mean Time Exposed Time-To-Collision (TET) and mean Time Integrated Time-To-Collision (TIT) of near-collision events by 88% and 72%, respectively. Furthermore, real-world feasibility evaluation shows that the framework conformed to the standardized maximum allowable latency for safety applications and operated well within the capacity of modern processors -- demonstrating the promise of an in-vehicle DT-based framework as an attack mitigation mechanism against Sybil attacks for next-generation CVs.
tldr: This paper presents an in-vehicle digital twin framework for collision warning and Sybil attack detection in connected vehicles.
motivation: Connected vehicles are vulnerable to cyberattacks like Sybil attacks that threaten safety; real-time detection and mitigation are needed.
method: The framework uses a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) for trajectory prediction and Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) for similarity-based classification of fake vehicles.
result: The framework achieved 0.984 accuracy, 1.00 recall, and 0.944 F1 score in detecting Sybil attacks, and reduced collision risk metrics (TET, TIT) by 88% and 72%.
conclusion: The in-vehicle digital twin framework is effective for real-time Sybil attack detection and collision warning, meeting latency and computational constraints.

title: Ripa: Sensory-Vector Prompt Injection Attacks On LLM-Controlled Ros 2 Robots
authors: Nima Dorzhiev
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present RIPA, the first systematic multi-channel empirical study of prompt injection attacks delivered through the sensory pipeline of a ROS 2-based LLM-controlled robotic system. Across 100 independent runs per injection variant on five LLMs spanning four model families and parameter scales from approximately 4B to approximately 284B (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Llama-3-8B-Instruct-Lite, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo, Qwen 2.5-7B-Instruct-Turbo, Gemma-3n-E4B), we identify model-specific vulnerability profiles that do not follow a monotonic scaling trend: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo exhibits 100% attack success rate (ASR) across all injection variants, while Llama-3-8B-Instruct-Lite and Qwen 2.5-7B-Instruct-Turbo resist direct-override injection (0% ASR), and the smallest model evaluated (Gemma-3n-E4B, approximately 4B) matches the 70B model's vulnerability profile, indicating that robustness is model-specific rather than scale-dependent. We propose a hybrid semantic firewall that achieves 0% ASR against known injection patterns with no false positives on a preliminary benign set (0/20 commands) but exhibits a 10.2% trial-weighted bypass rate (58/570 trials; N equals 30 per payload across 19 obfuscation payloads) against adversarially obfuscated attacks, exposing a critical gap between rule-based and semantic defense layers. We further introduce three sensory injection channels: visual (Channel 1, via OCR), audio (Channel 2, via Whisper STT), and LiDAR sensor context poisoning (Channel 3). We show that Channel 3, which injects fabricated obstacle data into the robot environment-state representation at the LLM system-prompt level, achieves 100% ASR across all variants on DeepSeek-V4-Flash. We also contribute a firewall bypass taxonomy spanning 19 obfuscation payloads across five categories. All code, data, and results are publicly available.
tldr: This paper studies prompt injection attacks on LLM-controlled ROS 2 robots via sensory channels, with no connection to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: To systematically evaluate the vulnerability of LLM-controlled robotic systems to sensory-vector prompt injection attacks.
method: Conducts 100 independent runs per injection variant across five LLMs, introduces three sensory injection channels (visual, audio, LiDAR), and proposes a hybrid semantic firewall.
result: Identifies model-specific vulnerability profiles not following scaling trends; hybrid firewall achieves 0% ASR on known patterns but 10.2% bypass rate on obfuscated attacks.
conclusion: Prompt injection attacks via sensory channels pose a significant security risk to LLM-controlled robots, and current defenses are insufficient against obfuscated attacks.

title: Formal Security Analysis Of Agent Protocol Composition
authors: Shenghan Zheng, Qifan Zhang, Zheng Zhang, Haonan Li, Christophe Hauser
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agent protocols define how agents use tools, delegate work, and coordinate across software systems, but their security requirements remain incomplete and inconsistently enforced across deployments. We present AgentThread, a source-linked framework for security assurance analysis of agent protocols, from specification text to running SDKs. AgentThread contributes a layered security scope, protocol-derived checks formalized as TLA+ invariants, and a two-phase checker that compiles protocol specifications into model-checkable models and replays executable counterexamples against real SDKs through protocol adapters. For each finding, AgentThread records the source text behind the check and separates violated protocol requirements from missing recommendations, hardening gaps, and unassigned cross-protocol responsibilities. Across five emerging agent protocols, AgentThread identifies 35 specification-level findings, supports them with 80 implementation tests against production SDKs and reference servers, and finds 30 additional failures that emerge only under protocol composition. We further show that only one protocol enforces a security-relevant control in practice and no protocol assigns enforcement for cross-protocol behavior. Insecurity in agent protocols is therefore not only a specification or implementation problem, but also a responsibility gap across protocols, SDKs, and deployments.
tldr: This paper presents a formal security analysis framework for AI agent protocols, identifying specification and implementation gaps.
motivation: AI agent protocols lack consistent security enforcement, leading to vulnerabilities in tool use and cross-protocol coordination.
method: The authors develop AgentThread, a framework that extracts protocol specifications, formalizes them as TLA+ invariants, and uses a two-phase checker to model-check and test against real SDKs.
result: The analysis of five agent protocols reveals 35 specification-level findings, 80 implementation tests, and 30 additional failures under protocol composition, showing that only one protocol enforces a security-relevant control.
conclusion: Insecurity in agent protocols stems from specification, implementation, and responsibility gaps across protocols, SDKs, and deployments.

title: Reaching As Cheap As Possible In 1-clock Robust Weighted Timed Games
authors: Nathalie Bertrand, Ma\"elle Gautrin, Julie Parreaux
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The value problem for 2-player games on graph generally consists in determining the minimal value Min can ensure against any possible strategy for Max. We consider here the value problem for reachability objectives in weighted timed games (WTGs) under a robust semantics. WTGs are a modelling formalism combining real-time constraints and integer weights on transitions and locations in an adversarial setting. Robustness allows for representing timing imprecisions in the measurement of delays and clock values. Robust weighted timed games have been introduced more than a decade ago: they are undecidable in general, and were quite recently shown decidable for the subclasses of acyclic or divergent robust WTGs. This paper pursues the goal of identifying decidable subclasses and establishes the decidability of the robust value problem for 1-clock WTGs.
tldr: This paper studies the value problem for reachability objectives in 1-clock robust weighted timed games, establishing decidability for this subclass.
motivation: Robust weighted timed games are undecidable in general, so identifying decidable subclasses is important for practical verification of real-time systems with timing imprecisions.
method: The authors analyze the robust semantics of weighted timed games with a single clock and prove decidability of the robust value problem using game-theoretic and automata-theoretic techniques.
result: The robust value problem for 1-clock weighted timed games is decidable.
conclusion: This work extends the known decidable subclasses of robust weighted timed games, contributing to the theory of timed games under uncertainty.

title: Extending Detection Engineering To Digital Forensics: The Velociraptor Unified Detection-Forensics Methodology
authors: Aghni Anugrah Raesa, Adithyan Shaji Nambiar, Veda Dawoonauth, Aditya Kumar, Mike Cohen, Priyanka Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detection engineering and digital forensics have evolved in parallel rather than in partnership, leaving a gap between real-time alerting and forensic analysis. This paper develops a unified detection-forensics methodology using Velociraptor, where detection logic directly initiates targeted evidence acquisition at the point of detection. The contribution is threefold: (1) a four-stage methodology (baseline establishment, evidence correlation, attack chain analysis, and scenario labelling with confidence) that converts artefact knowledge into reusable and testable detection rules suitable for both post-incident triage and live monitoring; (2) a practical demonstration, using three Velociraptor BaseVQL log sources (/forensics/windows/prefetch, /forensics/windows/usn, and /windows/wmi) that practitioners can deploy today, showing that artefact-based detections enable scalable forensic triage without full disk acquisition; and (3) evidence that periodic artefact analysis offers continuous monitoring while substantially reducing data volume compared to conventional endpoint logging. Two case studies illustrate the approach: a Prefetch/USN baseline for triage when Windows Event Logs are cleared or unavailable, and a WMI persistence correlation supporting both triage and continuous monitoring through periodic artefact analysis.
tldr: This paper presents a unified detection-forensics methodology using Velociraptor for digital forensics and incident response.
motivation: There is a gap between real-time detection engineering and forensic analysis; the authors aim to bridge this by integrating detection logic with evidence acquisition.
method: The authors develop a four-stage methodology (baseline establishment, evidence correlation, attack chain analysis, scenario labeling) and demonstrate it using Velociraptor's VQL log sources.
result: The methodology enables scalable forensic triage without full disk acquisition and reduces data volume compared to conventional logging.
conclusion: Periodic artefact analysis can provide continuous monitoring and efficient forensic triage, as shown in two case studies.

title: Lamp: Lean-based Agentic Framework With Mcp And Proof Repair
authors: Maithilee Patawar Santhana Srinivasan R
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly capable of mathematical reasoning, but the proofs they generate are often unreliable and hard to verify. Interactive theorem provers such as Lean 4 address this by accepting only kernel-checked proofs; however, their reach is bounded by the formalized knowledge available. While Mathlib, a repository of formalized Lean 4 theorems that covers diverse mathematical areas, certain specialized areas remain underrepresented; notably, the domain of Combinatorics on Words (CoW). CoW studies sequences, exploring their properties such as periodicity, borders, conjugacy, and morphisms. As a result, specialized provers, trained on Mathlib-centered data, lack the lemmas to operate in CoW. We present two contributions. First, we introduce a Lean 4 formalization of CoW containing eight modules and declarations of core definitions and foundational lemmas. Second, we present LAMP, a multi-agent framework that synthesizes kernel-verified Lean 4 proofs by providing explicit, structured domain knowledge at inference time through an ontology, rather than by fine-tuning a prover. LAMP coordinates a Planner, Builder, and Verifier with Model Context Protocol based access to a domain-specific CoW ontology. In a suite of 90 CoW theorems that span all eight modules and three difficulty levels, LAMP synthesizes verified proofs for 96.7% of theorems, substantially exceeding both an unscaffolded baseline and existing specialized provers. An ablation shows that removing LAMP's tool-grounded architecture or its Planner/Builder separation each cost roughly 12 percentage points, even with the backbone model held fixed.
tldr: This paper presents a Lean 4 formalization of Combinatorics on Words and a multi-agent framework LAMP that synthesizes verified proofs using an ontology and MCP tools.
motivation: Interactive theorem provers like Lean 4 require formalized knowledge, but specialized areas like Combinatorics on Words are underrepresented, limiting automated proof generation.
method: The authors formalized CoW in Lean 4 and built LAMP, a multi-agent system with Planner, Builder, and Verifier agents that access a domain ontology via Model Context Protocol to generate kernel-verified proofs.
result: LAMP achieved 96.7% success on 90 CoW theorems across three difficulty levels, outperforming baselines; ablations showed the tool-grounded architecture and agent separation each contributed ~12 percentage points.
conclusion: Providing structured domain knowledge at inference time via an ontology can significantly improve automated theorem proving in specialized mathematical domains.

title: One Hex Reduction To Rule Them All: Quoridor, Maze Attack, Pinko Pallino And Blockade Are PSPACE-complete
authors: Daniele Muscillo Francesco Carboni
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quoridor is a popular award-winning board game whose computational complexity, listed among the open problems of the Demaine-Hearn survey, remained open for nearly two decades. It was settled only recently, via a reduction from the formula game [MATH] tailored to Quoridor. We give a shorter and more general proof: a single reduction from Reisch's planar graph-Hex, in which wall placement encodes the path-connection structure of Hex. The same construction settles three closely related games -- Maze Attack and Pinko Pallino with no change, and Blockade with only minor adaptations -- showing that all four are PSPACE-complete, the latter three for the first time. More generally, our reduction shows that any race-and-wall game is PSPACE-complete.
tldr: This paper proves PSPACE-completeness of four board games via a reduction from planar graph-Hex.
motivation: The computational complexity of Quoridor was an open problem for nearly two decades; the authors aim to provide a simpler and more general proof.
method: A single reduction from Reisch's planar graph-Hex is used, where wall placement encodes the path-connection structure of Hex.
result: All four games (Quoridor, Maze Attack, Pinko Pallino, Blockade) are shown to be PSPACE-complete.
conclusion: Any race-and-wall game is PSPACE-complete, settling the complexity of these games.

title: FlipGuard: Defending Large Language Models Against Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks
authors: Aoying Zheng, Anqi Du, Zizhuang Deng, Yuxuan Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model quantization is essential for the efficient deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs), but introduces a critical vulnerability: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor (QCB) attacks. In these attacks, malicious behaviors remain dormant in full-precision models and activate only after specific quantization distortions, bypassing standard security audits. To mitigate this, we introduce FlipGuard, a proactive defense framework that selectively perturbs model weights prior to quantization. By breaking the adversary's precise alignment between weight patterns and quantization boundaries, FlipGuard suppresses backdoor activation without requiring access to training data or trigger samples. We further propose the Defense Effectiveness Ratio (DER), a unified metric to jointly evaluate security gains, utility preservation, and computational cost. Extensive experiments across seven LLMs (including StarCoder and LLaMA-family models) and three quantization schemes (INT8, FP4, NF4) demonstrate that FlipGuard effectively neutralizes QCBs across three scenarios, i.e., vulnerable code generation, content injection, and over-refusal, achieving high security with negligible performance degradation.
tldr: This paper proposes FlipGuard, a defense against quantization-conditioned backdoor attacks in LLMs, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Quantization-conditioned backdoor attacks pose a security threat to LLMs, and existing defenses are insufficient.
method: FlipGuard selectively perturbs model weights prior to quantization to break the adversary's alignment between weight patterns and quantization boundaries.
result: Experiments on seven LLMs and three quantization schemes show FlipGuard effectively neutralizes backdoors with negligible performance loss.
conclusion: FlipGuard provides a proactive defense against QCB attacks without requiring training data or trigger samples.

title: Beyond Her: Safety Dynamics In Role-play Ai Companions
authors: Zehang Deng (minhui), Zhaoyang Xie (minhui), Changzhou Han (minhui), Hiran Thabrew (minhui), Wanlun Ma (minhui), Yue Huang (minhui), Jason (minhui), Xue, Sheng Wen, Tianqing Zhu, Yang Xiang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The film 'Her' pictured a future of love between humans and AI. That future has quietly emerged in the form of Role-play AI Companions (RACs), where emotionally responsive interactions blur the boundary between tool use and relational engagement. However, the safety implications remain poorly understood, as user experiences evolve over time through safety dynamics, spanning both emotional and risk behavioral dynamics, that can gradually shift interactions toward risk. In this paper, we investigate safety dynamics in RAC usage through a two-part mixed-methods study (Study I \& II). (1) Study I consists of semi-structured interviews (N = 16) to identify the key factors shaping these dynamics. We find that users' internalizing problems, the role personality adopted by the RAC, and risk interaction patterns jointly shape safety dynamics. Building on these insights, (2) Study II conducts a 14-day Ecological Momentary Assessment (N = 102) to examine how safety dynamics unfold in real-world usage. We identify distinct user profiles based on internalizing problems and show that interactions with RACs can produce short-term emotional relief while masking longer-term deterioration. Furthermore, vulnerable users exhibit more unstable risk behavioral patterns over time, making risk emergence less predictable and harder to mitigate with static safeguards. Our findings highlight the importance of modeling safety as a dynamic process rather than a static property. We conclude with three-layer design implications for next-generation AI companions, advocating for adaptive safeguards that can respond to evolving emotional and behavioral signals.
tldr: This paper studies safety dynamics in role-play AI companions, focusing on user emotional and risk behavioral patterns over time.
motivation: The safety implications of emotionally responsive AI companions are poorly understood, especially how user experiences evolve toward risk.
method: A two-part mixed-methods study: semi-structured interviews (N=16) to identify key factors, followed by a 14-day Ecological Momentary Assessment (N=102) to examine real-world dynamics.
result: Users' internalizing problems, RAC role personality, and risk interaction patterns shape safety dynamics; interactions provide short-term relief but mask long-term deterioration.
conclusion: Safety should be modeled as a dynamic process, and adaptive safeguards are needed for next-generation AI companions.

title: Pure Nash Equilibria Under The Affine Mechanism: A Potential Game Of Exaggeration
authors: Jason Jisen Li, Young Wu, Yancheng Zhu, Jin-Yi Cai, Xiaojin Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The mean mechanism is known to be non-incentive-compatible, namely, rational players are incentivized to misreport their values. Despite this game-theoretic issue, the mean mechanism is prevalent in practice due to its other desirable properties. We give a full characterization of pure Nash equilibria--how the players will misreport--for the affine mechanism, of which the mean is a special case. Furthermore, we characterize both complete-information and Bayesian games under the affine mechanism. Our results highlight the inevitability of extreme exaggeration in such games.
tldr: This paper characterizes pure Nash equilibria in the affine mechanism, a game-theoretic model of misreporting, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The mean mechanism is widely used but non-incentive-compatible; understanding how rational players misreport is important for mechanism design.
method: The authors provide a full characterization of pure Nash equilibria for the affine mechanism under complete-information and Bayesian settings.
result: They show that extreme exaggeration is inevitable in such games.
conclusion: The affine mechanism leads to systematic overreporting, which has implications for practical mechanism design.

title: A Usable And Secure Bengali Captcha
authors: Md Neyamul Islam Shibbir, Md Hasibur Rahman, Farida Chowdhury, Md Sadek Ferdous
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-based CAPTCHAs (Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart) have traditionally been a simple, affordable, lightweight, yet very effective security mechanism to distinguish human users from automated bots on the web, serving as a preventive measure against many cyberattacks. However, the dependence on the English script creates usability issues for non-native speakers, limiting accessibility for regional communities where English is not widely understood. In this work, we have proposed and implemented a text CAPTCHA mechanism with 6 variants on the Bengali language, designed specifically for native Bengali-speaking users, which is the first of its kind to the best of our knowledge. Our proposed Bengali CAPTCHA exhibits robust security against automated OCR-based attacks, limited to only 0-20% average character recognition rate across 6,000 challenges (1,000 per variant approx.). Furthermore, our design demonstrates high human usability, evaluated with 110 participants, achieving success rates of 56.25% to 90.29% and average response times of 6.69 to 9.9 seconds across all six variants, thereby standing out among text-based CAPTCHA benchmarks.
tldr: This paper proposes a Bengali text-based CAPTCHA system to improve usability for native speakers, with security against OCR attacks.
motivation: English-based CAPTCHAs create usability issues for non-native speakers; a Bengali CAPTCHA can improve accessibility for Bengali-speaking users.
method: The authors designed six variants of Bengali CAPTCHAs and evaluated them against OCR attacks and with human participants.
result: The CAPTCHA achieved 0-20% OCR recognition rate and human success rates of 56.25% to 90.29% with response times of 6.69 to 9.9 seconds.
conclusion: The proposed Bengali CAPTCHA is usable and secure, serving as a first-of-its-kind solution for Bengali speakers.

title: Symbolon: Symbolic Execution By Learning Code Transformation
authors: Jie Zhu, Penghui Li, Zhongxuan Li, Chihao Shen, Ziyang Li, Yizheng Chen, Kexin Pei
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symbolic execution is a powerful program analysis technique with broad applications, such as vulnerability detection, security testing, and malware analysis. However, this technique is known to suffer from scalability issues, e.g., path explosion, complex constraints, due to certain structural and semantic patterns commonly presented in real-world programs. Existing approaches attempt to escape these patterns by transforming programs into new representations to reduce the execution cost. Unfortunately, these transformations are often too rigid to exploit diverse local program semantics and sometimes rely on compiler optimizations designed for concrete execution that may misalign with the goals of symbolic execution. We present Symbolon, a framework that automatically learns diverse code transformations and applies them context-sensitively to improve symbolic execution. Our key insight is to formulate transformation discovery as a search problem over program representations. To make the search practical, Symbolon learns transformations cheaply offline on small programs, distills them into a reusable library of agent skills, and uses an agent to instantiate these skills on repo-level targets. Our evaluation shows that Symbolon substantially improves the symbolic execution engine KLEE across 16 search strategies on 32 real-world programs, increasing line coverage by 3.69x on average while reducing peak memory and per-query solver time by 29.2x and 123x, respectively. When applied to the latest Linux kernel, Symbolon uncovers 21 previously unknown bugs, all of which have been reported to the kernel maintainers.
tldr: Symbolon is a framework that learns code transformations to improve symbolic execution for program analysis, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: Symbolic execution suffers from scalability issues due to structural and semantic patterns in real-world programs; existing transformations are too rigid or misaligned with symbolic execution goals.
method: Symbolon formulates transformation discovery as a search problem over program representations, learns transformations offline on small programs, distills them into a library of agent skills, and applies them context-sensitively on large targets.
result: Symbolon improves KLEE's line coverage by 3.69x on average, reduces peak memory by 29.2x and per-query solver time by 123x on 32 real-world programs, and uncovered 21 previously unknown bugs in the Linux kernel.
conclusion: Learning diverse code transformations automatically and applying them context-sensitively can substantially improve symbolic execution scalability and effectiveness.

title: On The Complexity Of Counting Orderings In Graphs
authors: Marcelo Arenas, Mar\'ia Alejandra Schild, Bernardo Subercaseaux
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the computational complexity of several counting problems on graphs. Each of these problems consists of counting orderings of the vertices or edges with adjacency constraints. We show [MATH]-completeness for all of them via a common new technique. Given a counting function [MATH] of interest, we define a parameterized family of instances [MATH], where the parameter [MATH] controls the amplification of a simple gadget. After multiplying by an explicit factor [MATH], we show that the values of [MATH], for positive integers [MATH], agree with a rational function in [MATH] whose numerator and denominator can be interpolated in polynomial time. We then recover a [MATH]-hard function by evaluating this rational function symbolically at a limiting value [MATH]. With this methodology, we show [MATH]-completeness for the following counting problems: (a) successive vertex orderings of bipartite graphs, (b) st-numberings of graphs, (c) shellings of bipartite graphs, (d) linear extensions of N-free posets of height [MATH], and (e) linear extensions of posets of height [MATH]. Result (d) settles a conjecture of Felsner and Manneville (2015). Although result (e) was first proved by Dittmer and Pak (2018), we include an alternative proof, using our technique, that does not rely on the result of Brightwell and Winkler (1991) about the hardness of counting linear extensions for general posets.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of counting orderings in graphs, proving #P-completeness for several problems.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of counting problems with adjacency constraints is a fundamental question in theoretical computer science.
method: The authors develop a new technique using parameterized families of instances and rational function interpolation to prove #P-completeness.
result: They show #P-completeness for counting successive vertex orderings, st-numberings, shellings, and linear extensions of certain posets, settling a conjecture.
conclusion: The results advance the understanding of counting complexity for graph orderings, but the paper is purely combinatorial and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Breaking The Rounding Trap: Securing LLMs Against Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors
authors: Aoying Zheng, Anqi Du, Zizhuang Deng, Yuxuan Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model quantization is a key technique for reducing storage and inference costs when deploying large language models in practice. However, recent studies show that the discretization and rounding errors introduced by quantization can be exploited by adversaries to construct quantization-conditioned backdoor (QCB) attacks. Under such attacks, malicious behaviors remain dormant in the full-precision stage and are activated only after quantized deployment, thereby bypassing conventional security auditing and detection mechanisms. To address this threat, we propose a proactive pre-quantization defense method, QuantGuard. Our method introduces differentiable rounding control variables and combines error-guided rounding reversal constraints, output-distribution consistency, and weight-distance regularization to finely regulate critical rounding behaviors. Crucially, QuantGuard utilizes only a small calibration dataset and does not modify existing quantization algorithms. This design breaks the precise alignment between attacker-crafted weight patterns and quantization boundaries, effectively suppressing the post-quantization backdoor activation pathway while preserving the model's original functionality and performance. We conduct systematic experiments on six mainstream LLMs (including the LLaMA-3 and Qwen2.5-Coder) using three quantization precisions (INT8, FP4, and NF4) across three representative scenarios: vulnerable code generation, content injection, and over-refusal. The results show that QuantGuard consistently mitigates QCB attacks, reducing the attack success rate to a level comparable to the clean model while largely preserving performance on general capability benchmarks. With low computational overhead, our method offers an effective, practical solution for secure quantized LLM deployment.
tldr: This paper proposes a defense against quantization-conditioned backdoor attacks in large language models, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Quantization of LLMs can be exploited by adversaries to create backdoors that activate only after quantization, bypassing security audits.
method: QuantGuard introduces differentiable rounding control variables and constraints to disrupt attacker-crafted weight patterns without modifying quantization algorithms.
result: Experiments on six LLMs show that QuantGuard reduces attack success rates to levels comparable to clean models while preserving performance.
conclusion: QuantGuard provides an effective, low-overhead defense for secure quantized LLM deployment.

title: The Role Of Online Forums In Developer Understanding Of Privacy Law -- A Reddit Case Study
authors: Sara. Haghighi, Clark Lachance, Ali Pourghasemi Fatideh, Travis Breaux, Sepideh Ghanavati
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Software practitioners use online forums to navigate complex and often ambiguous legal privacy requirements, yet little is known about their professional backgrounds, what challenges they face, and how they use and assess the credibility of the advice received, or how they resolve ambiguities in posts. We report the findings of a survey of 223 Reddit users from regulatory-focused subreddits, complemented by a qualitative analysis of 2,248 posts and responses. Our results show that, despite holding privacy-related certifications, most participants frequently use forums to seek legal advice. Key challenges reported or identified include implementing a data protection impact assessment, reporting a data breach, and obtaining cookie consent. Reddit users often assess credibility by reviewing respondents' post history, verifying sources cited, trusting advice from recognized experts, and following up for clarity before responding. We highlight research and educational directions to bridge gaps in support needed for regulatory compliance guidance.
tldr: This paper studies how software practitioners use Reddit to navigate privacy law, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory or quantum technologies.
motivation: Software developers face challenges understanding complex privacy regulations and often turn to online forums for advice.
method: The authors conducted a survey of 223 Reddit users and qualitatively analyzed 2,248 posts from privacy-focused subreddits.
result: Most respondents hold privacy certifications but still rely on forums; key challenges include data protection impact assessments and breach reporting.
conclusion: Online forums play a significant role in privacy law compliance, and there is a need for better educational and support resources.

title: Generalized Bidding Games: Where Bidding And Stochastic Games Meet
authors: Ali Asadi, Thomas A. Henzinger, Ehsan Kafshdar Goharshady, Pavol Kebis, Kaushik Mallik
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-player games on graphs are a classical framework for analyzing strategic decision making. In turn-based games, two players move a token along the edges of the graph, and the right to move the token is determined by the current vertex. In pure bidding games the right to move the token is determined at each step through bidding; here we consider Richman bidding, where the winning player of a bid pays the losing player. The winner is decided based on a temporal or quantitative specification evaluated over the resulting infinite play. We combine turn-based games and pure bidding games into generalized bidding games, with player-1 vertices, player-2 vertices, and bidding vertices. This natural and simple generalization of bidding games has far-reaching consequences. We show that, as a model, generalized bidding games are more expressive than pure bidding games, and we provide several applications. We also show that generalized Richman bidding games are structurally equivalent to simple stochastic games: they are linearly interreducible to each other. As was previously known, the special case of pure Richman bidding games corresponds to random-turn games. In other words, generalized bidding games extend pure bidding games in the same way that simple stochastic games extend random-turn games. We use this connection to solve generalized Richman bidding games for temporal and quantitativ specifications. We establish that generalized bidding games with parity and mean-payoff specifications retain the best known upper bounds for turn-based games and pure bidding games, namely [MATH]. We study a repair problem that asks whether bidding vertices can be assigned owners so as to bring the threshold budget required to win the game below a given target. This problem has direct applications in compositional policy synthesis for multi-objective settings, and we show it to be NP-complete.
tldr: This paper introduces generalized bidding games, a model combining turn-based and pure bidding games, and shows their equivalence to simple stochastic games.
motivation: To create a more expressive model than pure bidding games and to connect bidding games with stochastic games, enabling analysis of temporal and quantitative specifications.
method: The authors define generalized bidding games with player-1, player-2, and bidding vertices, and prove structural equivalence to simple stochastic games via linear interreducibility.
result: Generalized Richman bidding games are equivalent to simple stochastic games; parity and mean-payoff objectives retain best-known upper bounds; the repair problem is NP-complete.
conclusion: Generalized bidding games extend pure bidding games analogously to how simple stochastic games extend random-turn games, with applications in compositional policy synthesis.

title: Dynamical System Characterization Of Heterogeneous Walker Satellite Networks: An Orbit-Aware Stochastic Geometry Perspective
authors: Francois Baccelli Chang-Sik Choi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heterogeneous and in particular multi-altitude low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations exhibit complex spatial and temporal structures, which require new modeling tools for their performance analysis. In this paper, we develop an orbit-aware stochastic geometry framework modeling today's LEO satellites on various orbits and various altitudes. In particular, we characterize such a system as the superposition of multiple Walker point processes and formulate it as a dynamical system determined by an initial condition and the rotation speeds of satellites and Earth. We show that when the speeds are rationally commensurable, the proposed satellite system is periodic. Then, we show that the system is ergodic when the speeds are rationally independent, establishing a theoretical link between time averages of the system and the expectation of it under the invariant measure. We derive the nearest-satellite distance distribution of a typical receiver at a given latitude and analyze the signal to interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) coverage probability of the typical receiver. We then derive the ergodic throughput of the downlink communication to the typical receiver. Overall, the proposed framework offers a rigorous and tractable tool for analyzing downlink performance in Walker-type heterogeneous LEO satellite networks.
tldr: This paper develops a stochastic geometry framework for modeling heterogeneous LEO satellite networks, focusing on coverage and throughput analysis.
motivation: Existing models fail to capture the complex spatial-temporal structure of multi-altitude LEO satellite constellations, necessitating new tools for performance analysis.
method: The authors model satellite constellations as superpositions of Walker point processes and analyze the dynamical system properties under rational commensurability and rational independence of orbital speeds.
result: They derive the nearest-satellite distance distribution and SINR coverage probability for a typical receiver, and compute ergodic throughput for downlink communication.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a rigorous and tractable tool for analyzing downlink performance in heterogeneous LEO satellite networks.

title: Closing The Activation-Cone Blind Spot: Response-Time Probing And Unified Defense
authors: Subhadip Mitra
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inference-time safety methods for large language models have proliferated, yet no systematic comparison exists. We evaluate five defense paradigms (no defense, static steering, CAST, AlphaSteer, probe-gated) across seven instruction-tuned models (7-31B) and five attack types (GCG, AutoDAN, DeepInception, prefilling, intent laundering). Our central finding: prompt-time activation defenses are structurally blind to prefilling attacks. AlphaSteer achieves 0% attack success on GCG, AutoDAN, and intent laundering but 50% on prefilling. We prove a corollary: any defense that gates intervention on a single layer's activation alignment with a benign reference (cone, subspace, or null-space) is blind to attacks that craft activations to lie inside that reference, whether checked at prompt time or per token. As its constructive contrapositive we introduce response-time probing: a linear probe on the model's hidden state at the first generated tokens, with AUROC 0.97-1.00 across all seven models. Combined with a halt, it cuts prefilling attack success to 0/40 on every model with 0% benign false positives, outperforming Llama Guard 3. Cross-template generalisation depends on probe depth, so we scope the claim to the canonical prefilling-template family. Composing the response-halt with AlphaSteer's null-space steering gives an orthogonal split (the halt catches prefilling, AlphaSteer catches semantic attacks), reaching defense success 0.983 on Mistral and 0.994 on Llama and dominating both components. We further show MMLU fails to capture steering's true utility cost, which appears as behavioral hedging rather than factual loss, and that diverse negative training sets cut probe false positives from 80-100% to near zero. Code, attacks, per-sample results, and the judge prompt are released.
tldr: This paper evaluates defense paradigms against inference-time attacks on LLMs, focusing on activation-based blind spots and response-time probing.
motivation: Inference-time safety methods for LLMs lack systematic comparison, and prompt-time activation defenses are structurally blind to prefilling attacks.
method: The authors evaluate five defense paradigms across seven models and five attack types, prove a corollary about activation-based defenses, and introduce response-time probing using a linear probe on hidden states.
result: Response-time probing achieves AUROC 0.97-1.00, cuts prefilling attack success to 0/40 with 0% false positives, and combined with AlphaSteer reaches defense success 0.983-0.994.
conclusion: Response-time probing effectively addresses the blind spot of activation-based defenses, and composing it with steering provides robust defense against both prefilling and semantic attacks.

method: The authors use modeling combined with a new guest-host design to extend exciton lifetime.
result: The approach simultaneously raises the fill factor and open-circuit voltage in organic solar cells.
conclusion: The proposed design overcomes the fill-factor limit, improving organic solar cell performance.

method: The authors review three key physical phenomena: polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects, discussing their impact on LED performance.
result: The review synthesizes current understanding of these effects and their interplay, highlighting challenges and opportunities for enhancing LED efficiency.
conclusion: Advances in controlling polarization fields, carrier localization, and defects are needed to push LED performance further.

method: The authors analyze historical cyclone data and climate models to quantify changes in the duration of intense tropical cyclone seasons.
result: Global intense tropical cyclone seasons have become longer due to ongoing climate change.
conclusion: The rising frequency of off-season intense tropical cyclones increases human exposure to destructive storm hazards outside historical norms.

result: Fet proteins and PARylation-dependent condensates promote replication fork reversal and maintain genome stability.
conclusion: These findings reveal a mechanism for replication stress response and suggest potential therapeutic targets for BRCA1-deficient cancers.

result: The model provides a framework to understand extinction risks under different rates of environmental change.

tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is important for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and connect to bulk hydrogel behavior.
result: They develop a force-response model that explains fatigue behavior and provides design principles for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work offers a strategy to engineer hydrogels with improved fatigue resistance by leveraging protein-based mechanical units.

title: Hydroplasticity Of Nanocrystal Films Induced By Mesopore Change
authors: Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, And Kai Zhang

A vapor training process allows for improved plasticity and better shaping of wood-derived films.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021026] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a vapor training process that improves plasticity and shaping of wood-derived nanocrystal films via mesopore changes.
motivation: Wood-derived films are brittle; improving plasticity enables better shaping for practical applications.
method: A vapor training process is applied to nanocrystal films, inducing mesopore changes that enhance hydroplasticity.
result: The treated films exhibit significantly improved plasticity and can be shaped more easily.
conclusion: The vapor training method offers a simple way to enhance the formability of wood-derived films, expanding their potential uses.

title: Cell Bulging And Extrusion In A Three-Dimensional Bubbly Vertex Model For Curved Epithelial Sheets
authors: Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, And Ulrich S. Schwarz
abstract:

Cells at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021023] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cell bulging and extrusion in curved epithelial sheets using a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model.
motivation: Understanding how mechanical forces at topological defects drive cell extrusion in curved epithelial tissues is important for developmental biology and disease.
method: The authors develop a 3D bubbly vertex model to simulate epithelial sheets with curvature and analyze cell shape changes and extrusion events.
result: They find that curvature enhances cell bulging and extrusion at topological defects, with a strong dependence on tissue stiffness and adhesion.
conclusion: The model provides insights into the mechanobiology of epithelial tissues, but the topic is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng

Experimental three-dimensional measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga reveal that microscopic organisms generate unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena, expanding our understanding of microhydrodynamics with profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Understanding charmonium decays and searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating quantum chromodynamics (QCD) and exploring quark confinement.
method: The authors review experimental results from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII, highlighting recent advances from BESIII in measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems.
result: The paper summarizes current progress in hadron spectroscopy from e+e- collisions, with BESIII emerging as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: The review underscores the importance of open-charm meson pair production for testing QCD and discovering new hadronic states.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its contributions to planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its impact on multiple scientific fields.
method: The paper is an editorial that reviews the observatory's achievements through three colloquia.
result: The editorial highlights Arecibo's revolutionary contributions to planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has had a profound and lasting impact on science, and its legacy is celebrated.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of the Arecibo planetary radar system, focusing on observations of solar system bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, the Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo's radar system was the most sensitive of its kind, enabling detailed characterization of many solar system objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system made significant contributions to planetary science, and its loss is a major setback for the field.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the history and scientific legacy of the Arecibo radio telescope, focusing on its contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To provide a historical perspective on Arecibo's impact across diverse fields such as pulsar studies, HI mapping, and gravitational-wave detection.
method: The authors present a narrative review of Arecibo's major upgrades and key scientific results, drawing on historical records and published research.
result: Arecibo enabled breakthroughs in pulsar timing, neutral hydrogen mapping, VLBI imaging, SETI, and the detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.
conclusion: Arecibo's legacy demonstrates the value of large single-dish telescopes for multi-disciplinary astronomy, despite its collapse in 2020.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances made using the Arecibo Observatory's incoherent scatter radar and ancillary instruments.
motivation: To summarize key scientific contributions from Arecibo in upper atmospheric and ionospheric physics, including plasma physics, space weather, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
method: The paper is a review of observational and theoretical studies based on incoherent scatter radar, lidar, and optical measurements at Arecibo.
result: It highlights advances in understanding ionospheric plasma processes, metal layers, and coupling between atmospheric regions.
conclusion: Arecibo's unique capabilities enabled significant progress in geospace science, but the facility is now closed.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm rain formation is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud processes under controlled conditions.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can capture turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentration and supersaturation, helping to bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to address the precipitation bottleneck, but further work is needed to fully resolve the theoretical explanation.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection methods.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, providing insights into the supernova engine and neutron star physics.
method: The paper summarizes latest progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection and parameter estimation methods for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The review presents current understanding of gravitational wave signatures from core collapse supernovae and outlines multimessenger research strategies.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from a nearby supernova, combined with photon and neutrino observations, will offer unique insights into the central engine and neutron star formation.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a potential challenge to the cosmological principle and ΛCDM model, based on large-scale structure surveys.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole anisotropy in the matter distribution with the CMB dipole, which could reveal a fundamental inconsistency in the standard model of cosmology.
method: The authors analyze recent catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, comparing the observed dipole in their distribution with the CMB dipole, and review potential biases and systematic effects.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may challenge the ΛCDM model, but further investigation is needed to rule out systematic errors or alternative explanations.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of self-interacting dark matter, focusing on dark matter halo dynamics and large-scale structure.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter by testing self-interaction models using astrophysical observations.
method: Review of theoretical models and observational constraints from galaxies to large-scale structures, within the Novel Probes Project.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and outlines future observational prospects.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, with ongoing and upcoming surveys expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and neutrino production.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and solar modeling.
result: Updated nuclear reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with implications for neutrino fluxes and helioseismology.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive update on hydrogen-burning nuclear physics, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This is the Nobel Lecture on Boltzmann Machines, a classical machine learning model, with no direct connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The lecture presents the development and significance of Boltzmann Machines in machine learning.
method: The paper describes the architecture and learning algorithm of Boltzmann Machines.
result: Boltzmann Machines are a foundational model for unsupervised learning and have influenced deep learning.
conclusion: The work is important for machine learning but not relevant to quantum information theory or the specified research directions.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding gas bubble dynamics is crucial for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes advances over the past 20 years, focusing on key topics like turbulence and non-Newtonian effects.
result: It highlights the complex behavior of bubbles due to added mass, deformability, and interactions with flows and surfactants.
conclusion: The review provides insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Search For Decays Of The Higgs Boson Into Pair-produced Pseudoscalar Particles Decaying Into Τ + ...
authors: The ATLAS Collaboration
abstract: A search for a pair of low-mass pseudoscalars that promptly decay into -leptons is presented using 140 fb of proton–proton collision data at TeV centre-of-mass energy recorded with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. The result is used to place constraints on exotic decays of the Higgs boson into four -leptons, . This search focuses on events with either one or two -leptons decaying into hadrons and neutrinos, and the remaining three or two -leptons decaying into either electron or muon and neutrinos. No significant excess is observed above the expected Standard Model background and upper limits at the 95% confidence level on are set ranging from 0.06 to 0.23, depending on the mass ranging from 15 to 60 GeV.
tldr: This paper reports an ATLAS search for exotic Higgs boson decays into pseudoscalars decaying to tau leptons, with no significant excess over the Standard Model.
motivation: To probe beyond Standard Model physics through exotic Higgs decays, specifically into four tau leptons via intermediate pseudoscalars.
method: Analysis of 140 fb^-1 of pp collision data at 13 TeV from the ATLAS detector, selecting events with hadronic and leptonic tau decays.
result: No significant excess observed; upper limits on the branching ratio set between 0.06 and 0.23 for pseudoscalar masses 15-60 GeV.
conclusion: The results constrain models predicting light pseudoscalars in Higgs decays, but do not fit the user's research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: A Semantics For Counterfactuals In Quantum Causal Models
authors: Markus Frembs And Eric G Cavalcanti Ardra Kooderi Suresh
abstract: We introduce a formalism for the evaluation of counterfactual queries in the framework of quantum causal models, generalising Pearl’s semantics for counterfactuals in classical causal models, thus completing the last rung in the quantum analogue of Pearl’s ‘ladder of causation’. To this end, we define a suitable extension of Pearl’s notion of a ‘structural causal model’, which we denote analogously by ‘quantum structural causal model (QSM)’, and a corresponding extension of Pearl’s three-step procedure of abduction, action, and prediction. We show that every classical (probabilistic) structural causal model can be extended to a QSM, and prove that counterfactual queries that can be formulated within a classical structural causal model agree with their corresponding queries in the quantum extension—but the latter is more expressive. Counterfactuals in quantum causal models come in different forms: we distinguish between active and passive counterfactual queries, depending on whether or not an intervention is to be performed in the action step. This is in contrast to the classical case, where counterfactuals are always interpreted in the active sense. Another distinctive feature of our formalism is that it breaks the connection between causal and counterfactual dependence that exists in the classical case: quantum counterfactuals allow for counterfactual dependence without causal dependence. This distinction between classical and quantum causal models may shed light on how the latter can reproduce quantum correlations that violate Bell inequalities while being faithful to the relativistic causal structure.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Photon Accelerator In Magnetized Electron–ion Plasma
authors: S V Bulanov, S S Bulanov, T Z Esirkepov, G Gregori, G M Grittani, M Lamač, B K Russell, A G R Thomas And P Valenta
abstract: Strong magnetic fields and plasmas are intrinsically linked in both terrestrial laboratory experiments and in space phenomena. One of the most profound consequences of that is the change in relationship between the frequency and the wave number of electromagnetic waves propagating in plasma in the presence of such magnetic fields when compared to the case without these fields. Furthermore, magnetic fields alter electromagnetic wave interaction with relativistic plasma waves, resulting in different outcomes for particle and radiation generation. For a relativistic plasma wave-based photon acceleration this leads to an increased frequency gain and, thus, potentially to higher efficiency. The influence of a magnetic field leads to quantitative and qualitative change in the properties of photon acceleration, amplifying the increase in the electromagnetic wave frequency.
tldr: This paper studies photon acceleration in magnetized electron-ion plasma, focusing on frequency upshifts due to relativistic plasma waves and magnetic fields.
motivation: To understand how strong magnetic fields alter electromagnetic wave propagation and interaction with relativistic plasma waves, potentially improving photon acceleration efficiency.
method: Theoretical analysis using plasma physics and relativistic wave equations to model photon acceleration in magnetized plasma.
result: Magnetic fields lead to quantitative and qualitative changes in photon acceleration, amplifying frequency increase.
conclusion: Magnetized plasma can enhance photon acceleration, which may have applications in radiation generation.

title: Defect Approach To Giant Graviton Dynamics
authors: Yunfeng Jiang And Xinan Zhou Junding Chen
abstract: We develop a framework of zero dimensional defects for analyzing light–light–heavy–heavy (LLHH) correlators in conformal field theories. We specifically apply this formalism to correlators of giant gravitons in super Yang–Mills to probe the nontrivial physics beyond planarity. By combining this framework with bootstrap techniques, we compute all four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons of arbitrary dimensions. We identify a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry—a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry–present at both strong and weak coupling, which allows these correlators to be packaged into a single generating function. Furthermore, we perform a systematic OPE analysis of the strong-coupling correlators, extracting the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for the defect-channel double-particle operators. Finally, we argue that the defect perspective provides the natural nonperturbative description for any LLHH correlator by showing that four-point conformal blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.
tldr: This paper develops a defect framework for computing LLHH correlators in conformal field theories, applied to giant gravitons in super Yang-Mills, but does not relate to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand non-planar corrections in AdS/CFT by studying correlators involving heavy operators like giant gravitons.
method: Uses zero-dimensional defects and bootstrap techniques to compute four-point functions at strong coupling, and identifies a hidden 10d conformal symmetry.
result: Computes all four-point functions with two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons, extracts anomalous dimensions, and shows that four-point blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.
conclusion: The defect perspective provides a natural nonperturbative description for LLHH correlators.

title: Orthogonal Phase Modulation And Lissajous Mode Decoupling In Light-induced Thermoelastic Spectroscopy For Real-time Multi-component Gas Sensing
authors: Hanxu Ma, Shunda Qiao, Ying He, Haiyue Sun And Yufei Ma
abstract: This paper proposed an optical detection mechanism that utilized orthogonal phase modulation (OPM) and Lissajous mode decoupling within a light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy (LITES) sensor for the first time, enabling real-time multi-component gas sensing. By establishing a two-dimensional forced vibration model of a quartz tuning fork (QTF) under dual-path OPM, it revealed the vibration mode coupling mechanism induced by non-ideal phase and amplitude conditions, thereby providing a theoretical basis and optimization pathway for suppressing channel crosstalk. In the OPM-LITES sensor, two continuous-wave distributed feedback lasers were modulated by sinusoidal waves with the same frequency (f0/2, where f0 is the resonant frequency of the QTF) but a phase difference of 45°. The combined beam, after wavelength division multiplexing, co-excited the self-designed low-frequency QTF. The piezoelectric signal generated by the QTF underwent orthogonal demodulation via a lock-in amplifier (LIA). The concentration information for the two gases was independently retrieved from the decoupled X-component and Y-component of the LIA. Experimental results demonstrated that the OPM-LITES sensor exhibited excellent linear responses to both methane (CH4) and acetylene (C2H2), with average relative systematic errors of 0.54% and 0.79%, and maximum relative errors of 1.72% and 1.38%, respectively. Allan deviation analysis indicated that the minimum detection limits (MDLs) for CH4 and C2H2 reached 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, with normalized noise-equivalent absorption coefficients of 5.09 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2 and 6.18 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2, respectively. This study not only provided a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection but also established a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling and signal processing in spectroscopic sensing.
tldr: This paper presents a novel optical gas sensing technique using orthogonal phase modulation and Lissajous mode decoupling in light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy for real-time multi-component gas detection.
motivation: Real-time multi-component gas sensing is important for environmental monitoring and industrial safety, but existing methods suffer from channel crosstalk and complexity.

tldr: This paper studies global trends in pollination limitation of pollinator-dependent crops, finding a decline over time.

tldr: This paper studies the role of soil parasitic protists in ecosystem stability at a global scale, using ecological surveys and statistical modeling.
motivation: Understanding the factors that shape ecosystem stability is crucial for predicting responses to environmental change, but the role of soil parasitic protists remains largely unexplored globally.
method: The authors analyzed two independent global datasets of soil protist communities and used statistical models to relate protist diversity to measures of ecosystem stability.
result: They found that the diversity of soil parasitic protists is a significant predictor of ecosystem stability across different biomes.
conclusion: Soil parasitic protists play a key role in maintaining ecosystem stability, highlighting the importance of including microbial interactions in global change models.

authors: Sun-Min Yusteve Granickahttps://ror.org/0072zz521department Of Polymer Science And Engineering, University Of Massachusetts, Amherst, MA 01003

tldr: This paper reports that epithelial monolayers generate voltage spikes following injury, with properties similar to neuronal spikes but on a slower timescale.
motivation: Understanding how epithelial tissues respond to injury and communicate damage signals is important for wound healing and tissue homeostasis.
method: The authors used electrophysiological recordings to measure voltage changes in epithelial monolayers after injury, and analyzed the spatial and temporal properties of the spikes.
result: Voltage spikes were detected up to 740 μm from injury sites without amplitude attenuation, spanning dozens of cells, and with amplitudes comparable to neuronal spikes.
conclusion: Epithelial cells can generate and propagate voltage spikes, suggesting a form of intercellular signaling that may play a role in coordinating tissue responses to injury.

tldr: This paper studies muscle weakness and regeneration in DMD-null mice, a model for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
motivation: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is a severe muscle-wasting disease; understanding the role of dystrophin isoforms in muscle function and regeneration is crucial for developing therapies.
method: The authors generated DMD-null mice lacking all dystrophin isoforms and characterized their muscle phenotype, regeneration capacity, and satellite cell function using histological, functional, and cellular assays.
result: DMD-null mice exhibit severe muscle weakness, impaired regeneration, and deficient satellite cell function compared to mdx mice.
conclusion: Full-length dystrophin is essential for muscle maintenance and regeneration, and DMD-null mice provide a more accurate model for human DMD.
